title: Trump to attend Phoenix semiconductor plant groundbreaking for Nvidia supplier
content: President Trump is scheduled to attend the groundbreaking ceremony for a new semiconductor manufacturing facility in Phoenix. The site will produce chips, including those for Nvidia, a company that recently drew attention due to the ouster and subsequent reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang. A White House official confirmed to The Hill that the President will deliver remarks at the event for the multi-billion dollar project.
summary: President Trump is set to attend the groundbreaking of a Phoenix facility that will manufacture semiconductor chips, including for Nvidia. A White House official stated that Trump will deliver remarks at the ceremony for the new multi-billion dollar project.
author: The Hill

title: IISS Report: Russian Sabotage in Europe Up 16%, Warns of Mass-Casualty Risk
content: A new report by the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) indicates that sabotage incidents blamed on Russia in Europe rose 16 percent year-over-year in September. The analysis warns of the potential for a future “mass-casualty” event by Moscow, noting that the Kremlin’s “unconventional war” on Europe has included attacks on critical infrastructure.
summary: A new IISS report states that incidents of sabotage blamed on Russia in Europe increased by 16 percent year-over-year in September. The report warns of the potential for a future mass-casualty event as part of the Kremlin's unconventional war on Europe.
author: The Hill

title: Employees at GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games reject union
content: Employees at Rockstar Games, the developer of “Grand Theft Auto VI,” overwhelmingly voted against recognizing a union this week. In a Thursday vote, 75.3 percent of employees, or 1,163 team members, rejected recognition for the Rockstar Game Workers Union with the Independent Workers of Great Britain (IWGB). Meanwhile, 24.7 percent, or 381 members, voted in favor.
summary: Employees at GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games reject union.
author: The Hill

title: Meta whistleblower says gag order reminiscent of ‘1984’
content: Sarah Wynn-Williams, a former Facebook employee whose book warned about the company’s power, said a gag order preventing her from speaking about the tech giant was akin to the reality in George Orwell’s “1984” novel. “Control what people are allowed to remember or what they are allowed to know, and you control what they are…
summary: Meta whistleblower says gag order reminiscent of ‘1984’.
author: The Hill

title: 15 hospitalized in potential Thanksgiving food poisoning at Florida medical center
content: Miami-Dade Fire Rescue officials reported that fifteen individuals were hospitalized following a potential food poisoning incident at Leon Medical Center’s headquarters Thanksgiving event. Crews initially responded to reports of illness before the situation was upgraded to a Level 1 mass casualty incident, according to statements made to a local NBC affiliate.
summary: Fifteen people were hospitalized due to possible food poisoning from Leon Medical Center headquarters’ Thanksgiving event, according to Miami-Dade Fire Rescue officials. Miami-Dade Fire Rescue told a local NBC affiliate that crews responded to reports of potential food poisoning before the call was shifted to a Level 1 mass casualty incident.

content: Rep. Madeleine Dean (D-Pa.) said she believed “Pennsylvania deserves better” amid speculation that she may launch a Senate bid in 2028 for Sen. John Fetterman’s (D-Pa.) seat. She stated Sunday on NBC’s “Meet the Press” that she was taking her time to “seriously consider” the possibility of running. “I’ve known John a long time, and…
summary: Rep. Madeleine Dean (D-Pa.) said she believed “Pennsylvania deserves better” amid speculation that she may launch a Senate bid in 2028 for Sen.

title: Texas AG-elect won’t defend Ten Commandments classroom law
content: Texas Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson (D) stated he will not defend the state law requiring public schools to display the Ten Commandments in classrooms upon taking office in January. Johnson told The Dallas Morning News that he views the law as unconstitutional, noting that the court will have the ultimate say on the matter.
summary: Texas AG-elect won’t defend Ten Commandments classroom law.
author: The Hill

title: Ask this question before correcting a friend's health myth
content: A friend might tell you that you must drink eight glasses of water a day. That advice leaves out the fact that daily fluid intake comes from a variety of sources, including other drinks and food.
summary: The article suggests asking yourself a specific question before correcting a friend's health myth. It uses the common advice to drink eight glasses of water daily to illustrate that fluid intake also comes from other drinks and food.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Brainstem atlas identifies potential REM sleep center in humans
content:
Researchers have identified a potential REM sleep center in humans using a new brainstem atlas. The study focuses on REM sleep, a stage characterized by dreaming and temporary muscle paralysis known as atonia. This paralysis is absent in individuals with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD), who instead experience shouting or violent limb movements during the sleep stage.

The findings are significant because iRBD may serve as an early indicator of neurodegenerative conditions. Many individuals diagnosed with iRBD subsequently develop disorders such as Parkinson's disease or dementia with Lewy bodies, highlighting the clinical relevance of the newly mapped brainstem region.
summary: Brainstem atlas identifies potential REM sleep center in humans.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Frozen Shoulder Linked to Blood Sugar Levels in Diabetics
content: Frozen shoulder can appear suddenly, starting with mild discomfort and progressing over months to difficulty with everyday tasks such as putting on a coat or reaching into a cupboard. Recent research points to blood sugar levels as a possible factor in why some people, especially those with diabetes, develop the condition.
summary: Frozen shoulder can develop suddenly and become painful, making everyday movements difficult. Research suggests high blood sugar may be a factor, especially in people with diabetes.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Raw Milk Popularity Soars in Searches and Instagram, Influencers Promote Benefits
content: Raw milk has seen a surge in popularity, with Google searches and Instagram posts about it increasing markedly over the past decade. Influencers who claim the beverage offers health benefits have been a key driver of this trend.
summary: Raw milk has become increasingly popular, with Google searches and Instagram post topics rising over the past 10 years. Influencers claim there are benefits to consuming raw milk.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Swedish aid for contraception saves women's lives, new analysis shows
content: A new analysis by Karolinska Institutet, the ONE Campaign and the Guttmacher Institute estimates that Swedish aid for modern contraceptives prevented 1.3 million unintended pregnancies and about 1,500 maternal deaths in low‑ and middle‑income countries in 2024. The study highlights the life‑saving impact of Sweden’s support for contraception access.
summary: The analysis from Karolinska Institutet, the ONE Campaign and the Guttmacher Institute estimates that Swedish aid for modern contraceptives prevented 1.3 million unintended pregnancies in low- and middle-income countries in 2024. It also estimates that the aid prevented about 1,500 maternal deaths.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Liverpool Researchers Release Board Game on Oral Health Inequalities
content: University of Liverpool researchers have created a new board game that brings oral health inequalities research to life. The game offers students, health professionals and other stakeholders a hands‑on way to examine the social factors shaping oral health and access to dental care.
summary: University of Liverpool researchers have created a new board game that lets students, health professionals, and other stakeholders explore social factors affecting oral health and dental care access. The game offers opportunities to examine how these factors influence oral health inequalities.
author: Medical Xpress

title: CEDAR Researchers Investigate Sleepy Sickness Mystery in Vilhelmina
content:
Researchers at CEDAR have studied and perhaps found an important piece in understanding one of the biggest medicinal mysteries of our time: the Sleepy Sickness that swept over Europe in the early 1900s.  

During the 1920's, Sweden was one of the hardest‑hit countries in the world, with the highest number of reported cases in Västerbotten, and especially the inland community of Vilhelmina.  

The investigation into the Sleepy Sickness focuses on the historical outbreak in Vilhelmina, a community that recorded the most severe impact during the 1920s.
summary: Researchers at CEDAR have studied the Sleepy Sickness that swept Europe in the early 1900s. The disease hit Sweden hardest in the 1920s, with the highest number of cases in Västerbotten and especially in Vilhelmina.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Lab experiments suggest bat RSV can enter human cells, but existing antibodies block it
content:
Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe respiratory disease and accounts for many deaths annually.  

A research team led by DZIF scientist Dr. Wendy K. Jo and DZIF scientist Dr. Jan Felix Drexler at Charité—University Medicine Berlin, together with DZIF board member Dr. Thomas Pietschmann and Dr. Sibylle Haid from TWINCORE in Hanover, has characterized a virus found in West African fruit bats. The virus is genetically distinct from known RSV variants but belongs to the same viral family as RSV.  

Lab experiments suggest the bat RSV can enter human cells, but existing antibodies block it.
summary: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe respiratory disease and is responsible for numerous deaths each year. A research team led by DZIF scientist Dr.
author: Phys.org

title: Simple microscope enables new quantitative rock analysis
content: Rocks contain detailed records of Earth’s history, with the size, shape and orientation of their mineral grains revealing how rocks formed, deformed, and changed deep beneath the surface. Traditionally, extracting this information has required specialized equipment and time‑consuming analysis.
summary: The size, shape and orientation of mineral grains in rocks reveal how they formed, deformed and changed deep beneath the surface. A simple microscope opens new possibilities for quantitative rock analysis, reducing reliance on specialized equipment and time‑consuming methods.
author: Phys.org

title: Duisburg-Essen researchers find CO₂ shapes its own catalyst, favoring formic acid
content: Electrochemists at the University of Duisburg‑Essen used computer simulations to show that carbon dioxide can shape the surface of its own catalyst when the catalyst is restructured with voltage pulses. The calculations suggest this restructuring enables CO₂ to be preferentially converted into formic acid, as reported in Advanced Functional Materials.
summary: Electrochemists at the University of Duisburg‑Essen discovered via computer simulations that carbon dioxide helps shape the surface of its own catalyst when the catalyst is restructured using voltage pulses. The calculations suggest this allows CO₂ to be converted preferentially into formic acid, and the findings were published in Advanced Functional Materials.
author: Phys.org

title: RNA discovery reveals how gut bacterium adapts to intestinal mucus
content:
Researchers have highlighted the challenges of the human gut’s mucus layer, noting that it is a harsh environment for bacteria where nutrients are scarce and conditions are difficult. The study aimed to uncover how gut bacteria survive under such stress.

A team from the Helmholtz Institute for RNA‑based Infection Research (HIRI) and the Chair of Microbiology at Julius‑Maximilians‑Universität (JMU) in Würzburg, collaborating with scientists at Vanderbilt Health in the United States, identified a key regulator that enables bacteria to adapt to life in intestinal mucus.
summary: Researchers at HIRI, JMU, and Vanderbilt Health identified a key regulator that helps gut bacteria adapt to the nutrient-scarce mucus layer. The study addresses how bacteria survive in the harsh conditions of the human intestinal environment.
author: Phys.org

title: New technologies help Natural History Museum uncover 92 species in its transformed gardens
content: The Natural History Museum’s transformed gardens in South Kensington have recorded 92 species for the first time between their July 2024 reopening and the end of 2025. These new findings, which provide insights into London’s urban wildlife, include the emperor moth and small red-eyed damselfly.
summary: The Natural History Museum's transformed gardens in South Kensington are revealing new insights into London's urban wildlife. Among the 92 species recorded at the site for the first time between its reopening in July 2024 and the end of 2025 are the striking emperor moth and small red-eyed damselfly.
author: Phys.org

title: Sony WH-1000XM4C headphones drop to $198 for Black Friday
content:
Sony has re‑released its popular folding‑design headphones as the WH‑1000XM4C, offering them at a Black Friday price of $198 on Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart. The new model is described as “nearly as good as the pricier XM6” while being $100 cheaper than its October launch price. The headphones are available for $299.99 at the manufacturer’s website, but the retailer discounts bring them to $198 during the holiday sale.

The WH‑1000XM4C builds on the original WH‑1000XM4, adding a 10‑band equalizer in the companion app—an upgrade from the five‑band equalizer on the earlier version. Reviewers note that this change improves the mid‑range frequencies. Other enhancements include better sound quality, improved noise cancellation, upgraded microphones, multipoint connectivity, and a sensor that pauses playback when the headphones are removed.

Sony’s other flagship model, the WH‑1000XM5, is also discounted during Black Friday, with Best Buy offering it for $169. The XM5 features more microphones for noise cancellation and uses the same ANC chip as the XM4C, but it cannot fold as compactly, making it slightly larger for travel.

Consumers looking for a high‑quality, foldable pair of headphones can choose between the newly discounted WH‑1000XM4C and the lower‑priced WH‑1000XM5, both of which are positioned as strong options for the 2027 listening market.
summary: The fan-favorite folding design returns with the comfortable, slightly improved XM4C headphones. | Photo: John Higgins / The Verge Instead of purely looking forward with its headphone designs, Sony went back to its popular WH-1000XM4 design and made some improvements to make it even better.
author: The Verge

title: Top robot vacuums from Eufy, Roborock, and Dreame up to 60% off for Black Friday
content:
Black Friday discounts have reduced the prices of several top-rated robot vacuums by up to 60 percent, making advanced cleaning models more accessible. The sale includes a mix of basic units for quick cleanups and high-end systems that vacuum, mop, and self-maintain. Notable price drops include the Eufy Omni C28, which has reached a new low of $379.99, and the Matic robot vacuum, which is receiving a rare discount through bundle offers.

The Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Flow, the brand’s first roller-mop robot vacuum, is available for $549.99, down from $999.99. This model features 20,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, a retractable mop cover, and a compact design. Another budget-friendly option is the Roborock Q10 S5 Plus, priced at $229.99, which includes sonic mopping, automatic mop lifting, and a self-emptying dock despite lacking a multifunction dock.

For those seeking advanced navigation, the Matic robot vacuum is offered in two bundles: the Standard Bundle for $1,395 and the Serene Bundle for $1,595. The Matic is designed for cluttered homes with pets and multiple floor types, featuring onboard water tanks and dust bags to reduce maintenance. The Eufy Omni C28, suitable for smaller spaces like apartments, is available for $379.99 at Amazon and Eufy, combining strong mopping performance with a small self-cleaning dock.

Higher-end models from Dreame also see significant reductions. The Dreame X60 Ultra, which offers 35,000Pa suction and dual roller brushes, is discounted to $999.99 at Amazon, Best Buy, and Dreame. The Dreame X50 Ultra is available for $799.99 at Amazon, Dreame, and Target, while the Dreame L40 Ultra Gen 2 is priced at $474.98 at Amazon. The Dreame X60 Ultra and X50 Ultra are distinguished by their ability to climb thresholds, though the X60 Ultra handles high thresholds more effectively.

Other discounted units include the Narwal Flow 2, available for $899.99 at Amazon with a coupon, and the Narwal Freo X Ultra, which costs $399.99 at Amazon. The Roborock Saros 20 is sold for $989.99 at Amazon, Walmart, and Roborock, featuring 36,000Pa suction and a slim design for cleaning under low furniture. The Ecovacs Deebot X12 OmniCyclone is priced at $749 at Amazon and Best Buy, while the SwitchBot K11 Plus is available for $160 at SwitchBot with a code or $169.56 at Amazon with a coupon.
summary: The Verge reports that several top-rated robot vacuums are discounted by up to 60 percent for Black Friday, with the Eufy Omni C28 dropping to a new low of $379.99. Deals include models from Roborock, Dreame, Matic, and Narwal, ranging from budget-friendly options to high-end units with advanced navigation and mopping features.
author: The Verge

title: BYD unveils purple Whale minivan with estimated 559‑mile electric range
content:
China’s BYD has announced a new flagship electric minivan, the purple‑painted BYD Whale, with an estimated range of 559 miles (900 km) on a single charge. The vehicle is positioned as a larger alternative to existing minivans, measuring 17.3 feet (5,270 mm) in length, 6.5 feet (1,996 mm) in width, 6 feet (1,815 mm) in height, and featuring a 123‑inch (3,130 mm) wheelbase, making it bigger than the Honda Odyssey, Chrysler Pacifica and Toyota Sienna.

For comparison, Volkswagen’s ID Buzz delivered about 200 miles of real‑world driving on a charge in 2023. BYD’s announcement highlights the Whale’s projected mileage and size as a notable step in electric minivan capability.
summary: Electric minivans could be the ultimate in utility, with room for passengers, gear, and huge batteries. While VW's ID Buzz only gave us 200 miles of real-world driving on a charge in 2023, China's BYD has just announced a flagship purple peoplemover that can go an estimated 559 miles (900 km) on electricity.
author: The Verge

title: M5 MacBook Air gets $300 Black Friday discount on 13‑inch and 15‑inch models
content:
The latest Black Friday promotion brings the M5‑powered MacBook Air to its lowest price since Apple increased the model’s cost by $200 in June. Both the 13‑inch and 15‑inch configurations are discounted by $300 at Amazon and Best Buy.

The 13‑inch M5 MacBook Air, equipped with 16 GB of RAM and 512 GB of storage, is now available for $999—$300 off the regular $1,299 price. The same specifications are offered in the 15‑inch version for $1,199, down from $1,499. Amazon and Best Buy also list 1‑TB variants at $1,199 and $1,499, respectively.

Apple’s review notes that the M5 Air sits between the lower‑priced MacBook Neo—now $599 after a $100 discount—and the higher‑end MacBook Pro lineup. The Air’s faster chip, larger RAM, and 512 GB of storage make it suitable for multitasking and creative applications such as Photoshop and Premiere. It also features a higher‑resolution display, improved speakers, a backlit keyboard, faster ports, and a sharper webcam that supports the Center Stage feature.

While the Air cannot match the performance or premium displays of the MacBook Pro, including the newer M5 Pro model with a PROLED XDR display or any M6‑powered machines, it remains a capable choice for users who need a laptop for work, browsing, and occasional photo or video editing.
summary: M5 MacBook Air gets $300 Black Friday discount on 13‑inch and 15‑inch models.
author: The Verge

content: Besiktas supporters clashed with police in Batumi during a Europa League match against Israeli club Hapoel Beer‑Sheva. Fans were chanting and officers pursued supporters outside the stadium.

title: Moscow's VDNKh park opens 20,000‑sq m outdoor ice rink for winter
content: Moscow’s iconic VDNKh exhibition park opened its vast outdoor ice rink for the winter season on Thursday, 26 November 2026. The 20,000‑square‑metre surface winds around the complex’s landmark Soviet‑era fountains, welcoming skaters to the newly inaugurated venue.
summary: Moscow's iconic VDNKh exhibition park opened a vast outdoor ice rink for the winter season on Thursday 26 November 2026. The rink provides 20,000 square metres of ice that winds around the complex's landmark Soviet-era fountains.

title: Alaska friends deliver Thanksgiving turkeys from the sky to remote families
content:
Two friends in Alaska deliver Thanksgiving turkeys to families in isolated wilderness communities each year by flying.

Some of those communities are completely off the grid and are located about 50 miles from the nearest road.
summary: Two friends in Alaska take to the skies each year to deliver Thanksgiving turkeys. They deliver the turkeys to families in isolated wilderness communities, some completely off the grid and around 50 miles from the nearest road.

title: Kim Jong Un and wife watch Russian troupe performance in Pyongyang with minister
content: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un watched a performance by a Russian artistic troupe in Pyongyang, accompanied by his wife Ri Sol Ju and Russian Natural Resources Minister Alexander Kozlov.
summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un attended a performance by a Russian artistic troupe in Pyongyang. He was accompanied by his wife Ri Sol Ju and Russian Natural Resources Minister Alexander Kozlov.

title: Estonia set to shut all five road border crossings with Russia on Dec. 1
content: Estonia is preparing to shut all five road border crossings with Russia on 1 December. Ahead of the closure, long queues have formed at the border. Officials say the decision is driven by security concerns and could separate families and affect local businesses.
summary: Long queues have formed at Estonia's border with Russia ahead of the planned closure on 1 December. The decision, prompted by security concerns, could separate families and disrupt local businesses.
author: Euronews

title: Police officer chases wild turkey on New Jersey's Garden State Parkway
content: A wild turkey caused an unusual scene on the Garden State Parkway in New Jersey, prompting a police officer to chase the bird along the highway. The incident drew attention as the officer pursued the turkey on the busy roadway.
summary: A wild turkey caused an unusual scene on the Garden State Parkway in New Jersey. A police officer chased the bird along the highway.
author: Euronews

title: EU Kids Act faces scrutiny as 1 in 4 teens report cyberbullying online
content: Almost all European teenagers are online, with 96 percent of 15‑year‑olds using social media, though many report feeling unsafe on these platforms. Among EU children aged 12 to 17, one in four say they have experienced cyberbullying, and nearly one in three say social media has left them feeling stressed, sad or socially excluded.
summary: Almost all European teenagers are online, with 96% of 15‑year‑olds using social media. One‑fourth of EU children aged 12‑17 report cyberbullying and nearly one‑third say social media leaves them stressed, sad or socially excluded.
author: France 24

title: EU Defence Commissioner Kubilius warns budget cuts threaten major projects
content:
In a recent interview, the EU’s Commissioner for Defence and Space, Andrius Kubilius, discussed his perspective on the growing confrontation between Europe and Russia. The former prime minister of Lithuania, who grew up during the Soviet era, outlined his concerns about the security dynamics in the region.

Kubilius warned that proposed cuts to the EU’s future budget could jeopardise major European projects in defence and space. He emphasised that such reductions would threaten the continuity of these initiatives.

He praised the EU’s SAFE defence loans programme, describing it as “really very successful” for supporting European defence procurement.
summary: EU Commissioner for Defence and Space Andrius Kubilius says proposed cuts in the EU's future budget could jeopardise major European defence and space projects.
author: France 24

title: France faces water restrictions as study finds record global surface water decline
content: Tens of thousands of people in France are living under water restrictions as the country deals with a drought despite recent rains, according to the environment ministry. A new study released Wednesday revealed "the largest global decline in surface water resources recorded" since 1991, when data collection began, indicating that water insecurity is a global problem.
summary: Tens of thousands of people in France are living under water restrictions as the country deals with a drought despite recent rains, according to the environment ministry. A new study released Wednesday reported the largest global decline in surface water resources recorded since 1991, when data collection began.
author: France 24

title: Paris Paloma promotes second album 'The Fatal Flaw' exploring Greek mythology and AI
content: Dheepthika Laurent chats with Paris Paloma on set ahead of her Paris concert. The UK singer-songwriter and guitarist is promoting her second album, "The Fatal Flaw", an ode to Greek mythology, art and feminism. She tells us why this album is more personal than her first record, "Cacophony".
summary: Paris Paloma promotes second album 'The Fatal Flaw' exploring Greek mythology and AI.

content: At least 11 supporters of Bulgarian club Levski Sofia were injured in Marseille on Thursday. Skirmishes erupted between the visiting fans and supporters of hosts Olympique Marseille before their Europa League fixture.
summary: At least 11 supporters of Bulgarian club Levski Sofia were injured in Marseille on Thursday. Skirmishes broke out between Levski Sofia supporters and Olympique Marseille fans before their Europa League fixture.

title: Mélenchon calls for overhaul of France-Germany ties, warns of conflict risk
content: Jean‑Luc Mélenchon, leader of the France Unbowed (LFI) party and a presidential candidate for the 2027 election, said on Friday that he is “hostile” to German economic liberalism and to Germany’s dominance within the European Union. He added that France could be pulled into unwanted conflict because Germany’s expanding military strength makes it a “target” for other nations.
summary: Jean‑Luc Mélenchon, leader of France Unbowed (LFI) and a 2027 presidential candidate, said he is hostile to German economic liberalism and its dominance of the European Union. He warned that Germany's growing military strength could draw France into unwanted conflict as Germany becomes a target for other countries.
