title: Spain moves to contain diesel spill after tanker capsizes off Ibiza, one dead
content: Spanish authorities raced on Thursday to contain potential damage to Mediterranean waters after a tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel capsized off Ibiza. The incident left one person dead.
summary: Spanish authorities raced on Thursday to contain any damage to Mediterranean waters after a tanker capsized off Ibiza. The tanker was carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel and the incident left one dead.
author: France 24

title: Uganda to pull troops from Lubero after army chief's Walikale threat
content: Uganda’s army announced on Friday that it intends to withdraw its forces from Lubero, a town in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo’s North Kivu province. The decision follows days after army chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba – President Yoweri Museveni’s son – threatened to take control of Walikale, another North Kivu town, an action that sparked a diplomatic row between Uganda and the DRC.
summary: Uganda to pull troops from Lubero after army chief's Walikale threat.
author: France 24

title: Bihar legislator Anant Singh hosts 400,000-guest wedding for daughter Shivangi
content:
Anant Singh, a legislator in Bihar who faces a murder charge, hosted a wedding for his daughter Shivangi Singh and Georgia State University MBA student Rishikesh Kumar on Wednesday. The celebration, held in a rustic rural setting, reportedly accommodated 400,000 guests. Six helipads were constructed for the event and a feast was prepared by 500 cooks.  

The wedding’s cost has been estimated at at least $600 million, and the guest list is said to have included world leaders and celebrities. The scale of the event has been compared to the opulent 2024 wedding arranged by Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani for his son Anant.
summary: Anant Singh, a legislator in Bihar who faces a murder charge, organized a wedding for his daughter Shivangi Singh and Georgia State MBA student Rishikesh Kumar that included six helipads and a feast prepared by 500 cooks. The celebration, held on Wednesday in a rustic rural setting, hosted 400,000 guests.
author: Guardian World

title: Oxford's Pitt Rivers Museum displays seized belongings of Naga fighter Gaidinliu
content:
The Pitt Rivers Museum in Oxford has opened an exhibition of items seized from Naga freedom fighter Gaidinliu, marking the first public display of the collection. The objects were taken by British forces in north‑east India in 1932 when the 17‑year‑old Gaidinliu was imprisoned for leading an uprising against colonial rule. Colonial officers confiscated a range of her personal belongings while pursuing her through the Naga hills and valleys and sent them to the museum, where they remained in storage.

The exhibition features 27 pieces, including a basket of Gaidinliu’s notebooks that are said to contain her prophetic visions as the leader of a Naga Indigenous religion, as well as her clothes, bracelets and amulets. The display offers visitors a glimpse into the material culture associated with her resistance and spiritual leadership.
summary: The Pitt Rivers Museum in Oxford is exhibiting, for the first time, 27 items seized from Naga freedom fighter Gaidinliu. The collection, taken by British forces in the 1930s after she was imprisoned in 1932, includes notebooks, clothing, bracelets and amulets.
author: Guardian World

title: PCATI report says Israel institutionalised torture of Palestinian prisoners
content:
A report by the Public Committee Against Torture in Israel (PCATI) examined 42 complaints against Shin Bet interrogators over the past decade. The committee concluded that Israel has institutionalised the use of torture to extract confessions from Palestinian prisoners, noting that abuse is sometimes recorded in official documents or approved in advance as “special measures” for interrogation.

The report warned that the practice could cause irreversible miscarriages of justice as Israel moves to implement a new death‑penalty law that the committee described as targeting Palestinians.
summary: The Public Committee Against Torture in Israel examined 42 complaints against Shin Bet interrogators and concluded that Israel has institutionalised the use of torture to extract confessions from Palestinian prisoners. The report warned that the practice could cause irreversible miscarriages of justice as Israel moves to implement a new death‑penalty law targeting Palestinians.
author: Guardian World

title: Israeli strikes kill 16 schoolchildren in Gaza since start of November, ministry says
content:
The Gaza Ministry of Education issued a statement after an Israeli airstrike on a residential apartment in Gaza City killed sisters aged 15 and 13. The ministry said the attack was part of a broader pattern of violence that has left at least 16 schoolchildren dead in the territory since the beginning of November.

According to the ministry, Palestinian students were targeted for the third time in less than 24 hours, an escalation the ministry describes as a continuation of Israeli violations against children. The statement also noted that young people across Gaza are facing increasing bombardment and a growing struggle to secure food, clean water, and shelter.
summary: Israeli strikes have killed at least 16 schoolchildren in Gaza since the start of November. Gaza’s ministry of education said Palestinian students were targeted for the third time in less than 24 hours, reflecting continued Israeli violations against children.
author: Guardian World

title: Israeli judges urge prosecutors to drop Netanyahu corruption charges
content: Dropping of corruption charges against Israeli PM after unusual intervention could set damaging precedent The Israeli judges presiding over Benjamin Netanyahu’s corruption trial have called on prosecutors to end proceedings, a highly unusual intervention that leaves the attorney general facing a momentous political decision. The prime minister has been charged with bribery, fraud and breach of trust in three complex and overlapping criminal cases that hinge on his relationship with telecoms magnates and other wealthy businessmen. Ending the trial without a ruling could set damaging precedents for media independence and how politicians are held to account.
summary: Israeli judges presiding over Benjamin Netanyahu’s corruption trial have called on prosecutors to end the proceedings. Netanyahu is charged with bribery, fraud and breach of trust in three overlapping cases involving telecom magnates and other wealthy businessmen, and ending the trial could set damaging precedents for media independence and how politicians are held to account.
author: Guardian World

title: Norse Atlantic Airways files for bankruptcy, cancels all future flights
content:
Norse Atlantic Airways has filed for bankruptcy and cancelled all future flights, citing surging fuel costs driven by the Iran war that have severely damaged its finances. The Norwegian airline announced it is entering insolvency and posted a message on its website instructing customers not to travel to airports, a directive that also applies to passengers currently stranded away from home.

This sudden collapse occurred just one day after the carrier suspended its flights, issuing a warning that its financial situation had become critical. The airline’s decision to cease operations marks a significant disruption for travelers who were relying on its scheduled services.
summary: Norse Atlantic Airways filed for bankruptcy and cancelled all future flights after surging fuel costs caused by the Iran war ruined its finances. The airline posted a website message telling customers not to come to airports, including stranded passengers, a day after it halted flights and warned its finances were critical.
author: Guardian World

title: Victorian election 2026: Voters head to polls as Coalition aims to unseat Labor
content:
Voters in Victoria have gone to the polls for the 2026 state election, with live updates and results expected later tonight. The contest features Labor premier Ben Carroll and Liberal leader Jess Wilson each seeking victory in the state race.

During the campaign, federal figures were largely absent from the state contest. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese did not hold a press conference with Premier Carroll, while federal Liberal leader Angus Taylor conducted only one press conference with his state counterpart, Jess Wilson.

The coverage also notes that Labor party workers are distributing how‑to‑vote guides and that candidates are working intensively, acknowledging the difficulty of the contest. Observers point out that the campaign has been dominated by issues typical of a government that has been in office for more than a decade.
summary: Labor’s Ben Carroll and Liberal leader Jess Wilson are seeking victory as voters head to the polls in the 2026 Victorian state election. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese did not hold a press conference with Carroll, while federal Liberal leader Angus Taylor held one with Wilson.
author: Guardian World

title: Swedish government clinic re-assesses ADHD and autism diagnoses amid stigma concerns
content: A government‑funded clinic in Sweden is offering reassessments for individuals who feel their ADHD or autism diagnoses do not reflect their experience. While many view such diagnoses as affirming, critics warn that the clinic’s re‑evaluation process could increase stigma surrounding these conditions.
summary: A government-funded clinic in Sweden is re-assessing people who feel their ADHD or autism diagnosis does not reflect them. Critics say the re‑assessment could deepen stigma.
author: BBC World

title: The lowest price ever on the Canon EOS R6 II tops some of the best Black Friday camera deals we've seen today
content:
The Canon EOS R6 II has reached its lowest-ever price on Walmart, dropping from $2,298 to $1,713.95 as part of Black Friday camera deals. This reduction follows the release of the newer EOS R6 III model. The camera is highlighted for its strong performance in low-light conditions, featuring a 24MP resolution sensor, an ISO range of 100 to 102,400, and eight stops of in-body image stabilization. It also includes impressive -6.5 EV low-light autofocus capabilities. In a previous review, the camera received a rating of four out of five stars.

Other notable Black Friday camera discounts include the Nikon Z6 III, which is priced at $1,996.95, down from $2,196.95. This model features a 24MP sensor, an ISO range of 100 to 64,000, and sharp autofocus. The Sony Alpha 7R V is available for $3,298, reduced from $3,799. It is a full-frame camera with a 36MP sensor, an ISO range of 100 to 32,000, and advanced autofocus, having previously earned a four-and-a-half-star rating.

Additional deals feature the Nikon D850, described as a top DSLR option with a 45MP sensor, a native ISO range of 64 to 25,600, and weather sealing. The Canon EOS R5 is also listed, boasting a 45MP sensor, eight stops of in-body image stabilization, 20FPS shooting speed, and 8K video capability. Both the Nikon D850 and the Canon EOS R5 received four-and-a-half-star ratings in their respective reviews. The article notes that while high-resolution models like the Sony A7R V and Canon EOS R5 suit users needing maximum detail, the Canon EOS R6 II remains a strong choice for astrophotography and general shooting.
summary: The lowest price ever on the Canon EOS R6 II tops some of the best Black Friday camera deals we've seen today.
author: Space.com

title: Renée Slegers leaves Arsenal Women’s head coach role after six home draws
content:
Renée Slegers has departed her position as Arsenal Women’s head coach by mutual consent following a poor run of form. The 37-year-old, who had signed a three-and-a-half-year contract in January extending her tenure until 2029, stepped down after the team recorded six consecutive home draws in the Women’s Super League.

The results have left the club languishing in sixth place, trailing leaders Chelsea by 12 points and sitting eight points behind a European qualification spot. This performance falls short of the high hopes for a title challenge that had been set for the current season.
summary: Renée Slegers has left her position as Arsenal Women’s head coach by mutual consent following a run of six consecutive home draws. The club currently sits sixth in the Women’s Super League, 12 points behind leaders Chelsea.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Tyson Fury cleared by BBBofC to fight Anthony Joshua in Cardiff
content:
The British Boxing Board of Control (BBBofC) has cleared Tyson Fury to fight Anthony Joshua in Cardiff next month, resolving prior mental health concerns. The regulatory body confirmed it would license the bout after investigating comments made by Fury’s wife, Paris, who had previously stated that the boxer had been diagnosed with schizophrenia.

The BBBofC indicated earlier in the week that it possessed the authority to deny Fury a fighting license based on those allegations. However, the claim regarding the schizophrenia diagnosis has since been retracted, allowing the organization to proceed with granting the necessary clearance for the upcoming match.
summary: The British Boxing Board of Control has licensed Tyson Fury to fight Anthony Joshua in Cardiff next month. The board investigated and retracted earlier claims that Fury had been diagnosed with schizophrenia after comments from his wife, Paris.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Taurus Bay wins Grade Two John Francome Novice at Newbury, following Jukebox Man
content:
Harry Redknapp’s prospects of securing a Grade One winner this season were boosted at Newbury on Friday, where Taurus Bay won the Grade Two John Francome Novice. The horse, making only his second start over fences, defeated Royal Infantry by a half-length while carrying extra weight. This victory marks a significant step for the former football manager, who has long sought top-level success in his ownership career.

Taurus Bay’s performance follows in the footsteps of The Jukebox Man, who gave Redknapp his biggest win in last year’s King George VI Chase at Kempton. The Jukebox Man won that same race on his chasing debut in November 2024. With The Jukebox Man currently sidelined due to injury, Taurus Bay is positioned to serve as a capable substitute at upcoming festival meetings as the season progresses.
summary: Taurus Bay wins Grade Two John Francome Novice at Newbury, following Jukebox Man.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Ferrari Teammates Hamilton and Leclerc Clash Again Ahead of Qatar Grand Prix
content:
Costly on-track clashes between Ferrari teammates Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc have created tensions that cast doubt on the team’s ability to function in a title fight. The conflicting pair recently held talks to resolve their issues ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix, a weekend drawing intense scrutiny due to the recurring nature of their disputes.

Hamilton and Leclerc collided during the previous race in Las Vegas, just two weeks after a similar contest for position in Mexico cost the team a potential one-two finish. Team principal Fred Vasseur expressed fury over the Las Vegas incident, stating it displayed a lack of respect for the team and was unacceptable. These recent events have raised questions about how such conflicts might play out if the Scuderia is competing for a championship next season.
summary: Ferrari Teammates Hamilton and Leclerc Clash Again Ahead of Qatar Grand Prix.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Manchester United extend Bruno Fernandes contract to 2028
content:
Manchester United have activated a clause to extend captain Bruno Fernandes’ contract until the summer of 2028. By exercising this option, the club has avoided the risk that Fernandes could have negotiated a pre-contract agreement with a foreign club from January to join them on a free transfer next summer. The original deal was scheduled to expire in June.

Fernandes stated earlier this month that discussions regarding a longer extension were on hold due to the current context of the team and the club. He has previously turned down two contract offers from Manchester United.

The contract extension occurred on the same day that manager Mauricio Pochettino warned his players not to expect him to be “nice” as he works to improve the club’s fortunes.
summary: Manchester United triggered a clause to extend captain Bruno Fernandes' contract until the summer of 2028. This move prevents him from negotiating a pre-contract agreement with another club on a free transfer.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Gibbs-White and Jesus lead Nottingham Forest past Chelsea
content:
Nottingham Forest defeated Chelsea to climb to 14th in the Premier League, following their previous victory over Manchester City. Morgan Gibbs-White scored two goals, including a penalty, while Wesley Fofana endured a difficult match. The former Leicester City player, who recently faced criticism for an unsanctioned French interview regarding a missed penalty at Liverpool, was subjected to foul-mouthed abuse from Chelsea supporters who chanted, “You’re not welcome here.”

Fofana was also humiliated by Liam Delap before fouling the former Chelsea striker to allow Gibbs-White to score his penalty. The result secured a win for Forest, allowing them to improve their league standing amidst a challenging week for Fofana.
summary: Morgan Gibbs-White scored two goals as Nottingham Forest defeated Chelsea to climb to 14th in the Premier League. Wesley Fofana was booed by Chelsea supporters after previously making light of a missed penalty in an unsanctioned interview.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England seek historic All Blacks treble after Maro Itoje cites improved form
content: Maro Itoje says the team have used morale-sapping defeats this year to reach this stage but there is ‘more to come’ Offer England’s players a choice between a cut-price “Black Friday” deal and another super soaraway All Black Saturday and this week’s answer is unanimous. This may be an opportune moment to snap up pre-Christmas bargains on the high street but Maro Itoje and his side are rather more intent on securing a priceless little chunk of history. Never before in 121 years have England’s men beaten New Zealand in three consecutive Tests and the last time their opponents lost six times in a calendar year was back in 1949. During that distant annus horribilis the All Blacks ended up contesting simultaneous Test series against South Africa and Australia and lost them both; this time around there would be no such asterisk.
summary: Maro Itoje stated that England used recent defeats to reach a stage where they can achieve a historic three-Test victory over New Zealand. England has never previously beaten the All Blacks in three consecutive Tests, while New Zealand has not lost six times in a calendar year since 1949.
author: Guardian Sport

title: McNabney's late double powers Ireland to 38-14 win over Australia
content:
Ireland secured a dominant 38-14 victory over Australia in a Nations Championship match, with McNabney scoring a late double to seal the result. The win marked Ireland’s second consecutive victory against the Wallabies in the tournament, following a 33-31 ten-try thriller in Sydney in July. This performance extended Australia’s losing streak against Ireland to seven matches in a row.

Sam Prendergast was instrumental in the Irish success, contributing 13 points through five conversions and a penalty. His tactical kicking was described as world-class, orchestrating a blend of power and finesse. Other try scorers for Ireland included Henshaw, Timoney, and Baloucoune.

The article notes that while Australia started strongly, they were ultimately outclassed by Ireland’s class. The victory was characterized as more convincing than the previous encounter in Sydney, highlighting a significant shift in the dynamic between the two teams.
summary: Ireland defeated Australia 38-14 in the Nations Championship, with Sam McNabney scoring a late double and Henshaw, Timoney, and Baloucoune also crossing for tries. Sam Prendergast contributed 13 points, helping Ireland secure their seventh consecutive victory against the Wallabies.
author: Guardian Sport

title: BBC Sport explores why snooker is mentally challenging after Mark Allen discusses struggles
content: Mark Allen has recently discussed his personal mental health struggles, prompting BBC Sport to examine the psychological demands of snooker. The report investigates why the sport is considered particularly mentally challenging and outlines the measures currently being implemented to support players.
summary: BBC Sport examines why snooker is considered the most mentally challenging sport. The analysis follows Mark Allen's recent discussion of his mental health struggles.
author: BBC Sport

title: 490,000 US households without power after Thanksgiving storms
content: Thousands of U.S. households remained without power on Black Friday following Thanksgiving storms that struck the Northeast and West Coast. As of Friday afternoon, tracking website poweroutage.us reported roughly 490,000 customers without electricity. This total included nearly 201,000 in New Jersey and Pennsylvania, about 69,500 in Missouri, and roughly 60,000 in Maryland.
summary: Roughly 490,000 customers in the US were without power on Black Friday following storms that hit the Northeast and West Coast on Thanksgiving. The outage affected nearly 201,000 customers in New Jersey and Pennsylvania, along with tens of thousands in Missouri and Maryland.
author: The Hill

title: Sen. Deb Fischer's office says husband Bruce Fischer died by suicide
content: A spokesperson for Sen. Deb Fischer (R-Neb.) announced Friday that her husband, Bruce Fischer, died by suicide. The statement, issued by an unnamed representative, provided an update on the death initially reported earlier in the week.
summary: A spokesperson for Sen. Deb Fischer (R-Neb.) said Friday her husband, Bruce Fischer, whose death was announced earlier in the week, had died by suicide.
author: The Hill

title: Ontario Premier Ford Calls for US-Style Self-Defense Laws After Toronto Home Invasion
content: Ontario Premier Doug Ford called for Canada to adopt laws that further protect the right to self-defense following a fatal home invasion in Toronto. He made this statement on Friday after a 39-year-old musician was shot and killed during the incident on Wednesday. Ford stated on social platform X that standing up to home invaders should not be a crime, adding that he is calling on the federal government to act.
summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford urged the federal government to adopt laws protecting the right to self‑defense after a 39‑year‑old musician was fatally shot during a home invasion in Toronto. Ford said standing up to home invaders shouldn’t be a crime and called for US‑style self‑defense legislation.
author: The Hill

title: Prince William praises Diana Award after charity says it can't meet financial obligations
content: Prince William praised the impact of the Diana Award on Thursday after the charity named for his late mother announced it could no longer meet its financial obligations. “The Diana Award has recognised and encouraged thousands of young people who are changing the world for the better,” the Prince of Wales told ABC News. “I…
summary: Prince William praised the Diana Award on Thursday after the charity announced it could no longer meet its financial obligations. The Prince of Wales told ABC News the award has recognised and encouraged thousands of young people who are changing the world for the better.
author: The Hill

title: SNL sketch boosts bipartisan congressional push for unpaid caregiver support
content: A legislative push to support people who provide out-of-pocket care for their aging parents got a boost from a viral “Saturday Night Live” (“SNL”) sketch that sparked renewed conversation about the reality of gender disparities in unpaid caregiving networks. The comedy sketch “Sister” drew laughter when it aired Nov. 14, but its truth has…
summary: A viral “Saturday Night Live” sketch titled “Sister” has provided new momentum to a bipartisan legislative effort in Congress. The sketch sparked renewed conversation about gender disparities in unpaid caregiving networks for aging parents.
author: The Hill

title: Tiny Alarms Wins Shakespeare’s Globe Climate Playwriting Prize
content:
Timothy X Atack’s play, Tiny Alarms, has become the first winner of Shakespeare’s Globe’s new climate playwriting prize. The work centers on Tiny, a 12-year-old schoolgirl who is an alien ecojustice influencer. Her funny and disconcerting takes on the climate crisis go viral as she attempts to warn humankind of its impending doom, a mission that proves more difficult than anticipated.

The play was inspired by the real beliefs of schoolchildren who participated in creative writing workshops led by Atack. These sessions explored ideas about the far future, with the children expressing the feeling that theirs would be the last generation of humans.
summary: Tiny Alarms, written by Timothy X Atack, is a play about 12‑year‑old ecojustice influencer Tiny who is also an alien warning humanity of climate doom. It won Shakespeare’s Globe’s new climate playwriting prize and was inspired by real beliefs of schoolchildren from Atack’s creative writing workshops.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Dozens of Labour MPs warn PM not to block Rosebank oilfield
content: Warning of ‘lights out for Labour in Scotland’ as Burnham faces choice between warring factions over North Sea drilling project Dozens of Labour MPs in favour of Rosebank are putting pressure on the prime minister not to block the North Sea oilfield, warning that doing so could spell “lights out for Labour in Scotland”. As many as 80 pro-drilling MPs are considering writing their own letter to Andy Burnham after nearly 100 of their colleagues called on the prime minister not to allow the project to proceed. Scottish Labour leader Michael Marra has also reiterated his support for Rosebank, cautioning that “working-class people in vocational jobs” were threatened by the decline of the North Sea basin.
summary: Up to 80 pro-drilling Labour MPs are pressuring Prime Minister Andy Burnham not to block the Rosebank oilfield, warning of severe electoral consequences in Scotland. Scottish Labour leader Michael Marra supported the project, stating that the decline of the North Sea basin threatens working-class vocational jobs.
author: Guardian Environment

title: US Army Detonates Poison Bomb of Lead Azide Over Iowa
content:
The United States Army recently detonated a poison bomb of lead azide over the state of Iowa, a move described as deliberate by Steven Donziger. The attack occurred even though a safer alternative existed. For decades, the army had stored lead underground at a munitions facility in Iowa. As early as 2009, officials were aware that the lead was deteriorating and could explode on its own, yet action was delayed.

In March, the army finally hired a Georgia‑based company to apply a chemical spray that neutralizes the lead. The process produces a non‑hazardous by‑product that can be disposed of in landfills. This development was presented as a solution to the long‑standing problem of unstable lead storage.

Steven Donziger, a U.S.‑based human rights and environmental lawyer, authored the commentary. He also writes the “Donziger On Justice” series on Substack.
summary: The US Army detonated a poison bomb of lead azide over Iowa, despite a safer alternative being known. The army had stored deteriorating lead at a munitions facility since 2009 and only hired a Georgia-based company in March to neutralize it with a chemical spray, producing a non-hazardous byproduct for landfill disposal.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Focus Groups Suggest New Plant‑Based Tuna and Pea Chips for Local, Sustainable Protein
content:
Focus groups exploring plant‑based “tuna” and pea‑chip options have highlighted a demand for new recipes that emphasize local, sustainable protein alternatives.  

Respondents say they favor plant‑based products that are locally sourced, sustainable, minimally processed, and familiar, while also meeting standard expectations for taste and value.
summary: The research shows that consumers favor plant‑based products that are local, sustainable, minimally processed, and familiar. They also expect good taste and value.
author: Medical Xpress

title: PROLIFIC Risk Score Published in The Lancet Respiratory Medicine to Aid IPF Research
content: The Pulmonary Fibrosis Foundation and the Prognostic Lung Fibrosis Consortium (PROLIFIC) have released a paper in The Lancet Respiratory Medicine that describes the creation and validation of the PROLIFIC Risk Score. The tool uses blood biomarkers to predict disease progression in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
summary: PROLIFIC Risk Score Published in The Lancet Respiratory Medicine to Aid IPF Research.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Scientists identify brain circuit behind sensory hypersensitivity in autism
content: Scientists have identified a brain circuit that underlies sensory hypersensitivity in autism. The study notes that many people with autism spectrum disorder experience ordinary sensory inputs—such as a light touch or mildly uncomfortable sensation—as unusually intense or overwhelming, provoking disproportionately strong responses that make everyday activities difficult.
summary: Scientists have identified a brain circuit linked to sensory hypersensitivity in individuals with autism spectrum disorder. The research notes that ordinary sensory experiences, such as a light touch or mildly uncomfortable sensation, can provoke disproportionately strong responses, making everyday activities difficult.
author: Medical Xpress

title: New brain cell map shows use of distinct RNA versions of same genes
content: A new map shows how individual brain cells use different RNA versions of the same genes. In complex organisms such as humans, a single gene can produce multiple RNA molecules through a process called alternative splicing. These differently spliced RNA molecules, known as isoforms, may lead to the production of distinct proteins.
summary: A new map shows that individual brain cells use different RNA versions of the same genes. These alternative spliced RNA molecules, called isoforms, can produce different proteins.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Inserm Team Maps Entire Human Kidney Blood Flow in 3D Ultrasound for First Time
content:
A research team at the Inserm Institute of Physics for Medicine in Paris has successfully visualized the entire vascular network and blood flow in a human kidney for the first time. The study utilized a novel ultrasound technique developed in their laboratory, which had previously been tested in animals. This breakthrough aims to improve the understanding and diagnosis of kidney diseases associated with vascular defects and could potentially be extended to other organs.

The findings were published in The Lancet Medical Imaging & Theranostics.
summary: For the first time, a research team at the Inserm Institute of Physics for Medicine (Inserm/ESPCI Paris-PSL/CNRS) in Paris has succeeded in visualizing the entire vascular network and blood flow in a human kidney. This breakthrough opens up promising clinical prospects: improving our understanding and diagnosis of kidney diseases linked to vascular defects.
author: Medical Xpress

title: mRNA Ebola vaccine trial starts in Uganda
content: An experimental Ebola vaccine trial targeting the strain responsible for the current outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has begun in Uganda, announced by the country’s virus research institute on Friday.
summary: Trials of an experimental Ebola vaccine targeting the strain behind the current outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo have begun in neighboring Uganda. Its virus research institute said Friday.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Artificial protein activates defective insulin receptors and reduces blood sugar in mice
content:
A study published in Science Translational Medicine reports that an artificial protein can activate mutated insulin receptors and lower blood sugar in mice. The protein was designed to engage the faulty receptors that, in certain genetic diseases, fail to respond to normal chemical signals.

The research demonstrates a potential strategy for bypassing receptor mutations that impair normal signaling, offering a way to restore insulin‑receptor function in affected organisms.
summary: Researchers designed an artificial protein that can activate mutated insulin receptors. In mouse tests the protein lowered blood sugar, as reported in Science Translational Medicine.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Cancer evades immune attack by disrupting immune cell teamwork
content: Cancer evades immune attack by disrupting the teamwork of immune cells. The immune system’s attack on cancer requires more than tumor‑killing cells; it also needs coordinated effort where certain immune cells recognize danger, rally reinforcements, and train other components in a vast disease‑fighting network.
summary: The immune system attacks cancer through a coordinated effort of immune cells that recognize danger, rally reinforcements, and train other components. Cancer can evade this attack by disrupting the teamwork of these immune cells.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Bernie Sanders: Extreme wealth explosion is the major problem of our time
content:
Bernie Sanders, a US senator representing Vermont, has characterized the concentration of extreme wealth as the defining issue of the current era. In a statement, he asserted that few people have ever held so much wealth and power, describing the world’s ruling class as exhibiting unprecedented levels of greed and arrogance. Sanders noted that leaders globally are beginning to address these dynamics, highlighting a recent “Summit Against International Oligarchy” held in Paris.

The Paris gathering included elected officials and economists from various countries, among them four Nobel prize winners. The summit’s proclamation identified the explosion of extreme wealth as the major social fact of our time and warned that billionaires pose a threat to democracies. Sanders, who serves as the ranking member of the health, education, labor and pensions committee, is noted as the longest-serving independent in the history of Congress. He called for a collective effort to confront and defeat what he described as a powerful, greedy, and corrupt ruling class.
summary: Bernie Sanders argues that the concentration of wealth and power among a small ruling class represents a pivotal crisis for democracy. He highlights a recent Paris summit where elected officials and economists warned that billionaires pose a threat to democratic systems.
author: Guardian Business

title: Groundwork Collaborative claims Amazon’s Black Friday deals not truly discounted
content:
Progressive thinktank Groundwork Collaborative alleges that Amazon’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale deals deceive customers by advertising products as discounted when they were previously available at the same or lower prices. The organization’s analysis indicates that two-thirds of the sale items were listed at these prices just days before Amazon began promoting them as part of its holiday curation.

The report highlights specific examples of products featured in Amazon’s best deals selection, including an Apple Watch listed at $680, women’s Hunter yellow rainboots at $127, men’s UGG boots at $180, and a Carhartt beanie priced just under $20. Groundwork Collaborative states that these items were not actually cheaper during the sale period compared to their prior listings.

Amazon has disputed the claims made by the thinktank regarding the pricing practices of its holiday sales.
summary: Two-thirds of Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale products were priced the same or lower in previous months Groundwork Collaborative finds, a claim Amazon disputes An Apple Watch on sale for $680. A pair of women’s Hunter yellow rainboots discounted for $127, and a pair of men’s UGG boots, $180.
author: Guardian Business

title: Study Finds Denisovan Teeth and Unknown Archaic Human Lineage in Southern China
content:
An international research team, led by first author Song Xing of the Centro Nacional de Investigación sobre la Evolución Humana (CENIEH), has published a study in Nature. The study examined four fossil teeth recovered from two caves in southern China.

The analysis identified two potential human lineages from the Middle and Late Pleistocene. One lineage shows Denisovan affinities, while the other represents a more primitive lineage whose evolutionary identity remains unclear.
summary: An international research team led by Song Xing, a researcher at CENIEH, published a study in Nature analyzing four fossil teeth from two caves in southern China. The study identified two possible human lineages from the Middle and Late Pleistocene, one with Denisovan affinities and another more primitive lineage whose evolutionary identity remains unclear.
author: Phys.org

title: Storybooks Teach Children Perseverance Through Not Giving Up Messages
content: Many storybooks include messages about not giving up when facing challenges. This theme is not surprising, as perseverance is considered an important factor for both learning and long-term success.
summary: Many storybooks incorporate messages about not giving up when faced with a challenge. These messages highlight perseverance as an important factor for learning and long-term success.
author: Phys.org

title: Austria Faces 2026 Drought: Rainfall a Third Lower, Rivers and Groundwater Decline
content:
Austria experienced an exceptional drought in 2026. From the start of the year until the end of October, rainfall was around a third lower than the long‑term average.  

The reduced precipitation led to low river flows and lower groundwater levels across the country.  

The situation raises questions about the link between water availability and global warming. While a warmer atmosphere can hold more water vapor, this does not automatically translate into increased rainfall.
summary: Austria experienced an exceptional drought in 2026, with rainfall about a third lower than the long‑term average from the start of the year until the end of October. The low rainfall caused low river flows and groundwater levels, raising questions about the link between a warmer atmosphere, which can hold more water vapor, and rainfall.
author: Phys.org

title: HKU researchers find barrier that traps nucleic acid medicines inside cells
content:
Researchers from the Department of Chemistry at The University of Hong Kong (HKU) and their collaborators have discovered a barrier that may prevent some promising nucleic acid medicines from reaching their targets inside subcellular compartments.  

The findings, published in Nature Cell Biology, could help guide the development of more effective drug‑delivery strategies.
summary: Researchers from the Department of Chemistry at The University of Hong Kong (HKU) and collaborators discovered a barrier that may prevent some promising nucleic acid medicines from reaching their targets inside subcellular compartments. The findings, published in Nature Cell Biology, could guide the development of more effective drug delivery strategies.
author: Phys.org

title: AfD Leads German Polls with 28% Support Ahead of Christian Democrats
content: Germany’s far‑right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) is currently the most popular party in the country, with polls indicating it has the support of 28 % of voters nationwide. This figure places the AfD ahead of German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s Christian Democrats, who are backed by 20 % of the electorate.
summary: Current polls show Alternative für Deutschland has 28% of voters, making it the most popular party in Germany. This puts it ahead of Christian Democrats, led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who have 20% support.
author: Phys.org

title: Engineers reveal the interlayer elastic limits of van der Waals crystals
content: A research team led by Professor Yang Lu from the Department of Mechanical Engineering at The University of Hong Kong, in collaboration with Tsinghua University, has measured the interlayer elastic limits of graphite and hexagonal boron nitride. These two materials serve as representative van der Waals crystals. The study also revealed the physical mechanism that sets these limits. The findings have been published in the journal Nature Communications.
summary: Engineers reveal the interlayer elastic limits of van der Waals crystals.
author: Phys.org

title: Vagus nerve stimulation via oesophageal implant improves pancreatic cancer outcomes in mice
content: Researchers implanted an electrical device around the oesophagus to stimulate the vagus nerve in mice with pancreatic cancer. The stimulation slowed tumor growth and spread and made the tumors more responsive to immunotherapy, resulting in improved outcomes.
summary: An electrical implant around the oesophagus that stimulates the vagus nerve was used in mice with pancreatic cancer. The stimulation made the tumours more susceptible to immunotherapy, improving outcomes.
author: New Scientist

title: Physically demanding work linked to 20% higher dementia risk
content: A large study found that the type of movement matters for brain health. Recreational exercise was associated with a 24 % lower risk of dementia, while physically demanding work at the job was linked to a 20 % higher risk. The findings suggest that the context of movement influences dementia risk.
summary: A massive study found that recreational exercise was linked to a 24% lower dementia risk. In contrast, physically demanding work was associated with a 20% higher risk, indicating that the context of movement matters.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists find extinction risk in five deep‑sea species in Gulf
content:
The deep sea has long been considered a safe haven for marine life, but new genetic research suggests a hidden biodiversity crisis may be unfolding far beneath the waves.  

Scientists analyzing more than a decade of genetic data from five species of deep‑sea fish and shrimp in the Gulf discovered troubling signs of extinction risk in every species examined.
summary: Scientists analyzed more than a decade of genetic data from five species of deep‑sea fish and shrimp in the Gulf. They found troubling signs of extinction risk in every species examined.
author: Science Daily

title: Texas A&M researchers cut cost of experimental injectable glucose sensor
content: Texas A&M researchers have found a way to dramatically cut the cost of a key component in an experimental injectable glucose sensor while maintaining its performance. The new approach uses fluorescent light to measure glucose levels from beneath the skin, offering a potential shift in how millions of people monitor blood sugar.
summary: Texas A&M researchers discovered a way to dramatically reduce the cost of a key component in an experimental injectable glucose sensor without sacrificing performance. The technology uses fluorescent light to measure glucose levels from beneath the skin.
author: Science Daily

title: Study finds most mouse brain neurons are versatile multitaskers, not specialized
content: A new study challenges a long‑standing assumption about neuronal specialization. By recording activity across 43 mouse‑brain regions, researchers found that most neurons function as versatile multitaskers, responding to a wide variety of information, while a smaller subset remains dedicated to specific functions.
summary: A major new study challenges the assumption that most brain cells are highly specialized, showing they are versatile multitaskers. Researchers analyzed recordings from 43 mouse brain regions and found that while some neurons are dedicated to specific functions, most respond to a wide variety of information in distinct ways.
author: Science Daily

title: American Astronomical Society
content:
Astronomers have expressed strong opposition to the Federal Communications Commission’s recent decision to license SpaceX for its Starmind program. The American Astronomical Society stated it was “disheartened and dismayed” by the FCC’s approval, which permits the deployment of up to one million satellites in low Earth orbit. This initiative aims to establish space-based datacenters by housing AI computers in orbit.

The pushback highlights significant concerns regarding the impact on scientific research. The American Astronomical Society warned that the proposed satellites could disrupt astronomical observations. Additionally, other stakeholders raised concerns about the potential for increased orbital debris and broader environmental risks associated with such a massive expansion of satellite infrastructure.
summary: American Astronomical Society.
author: Guardian Science

title: NIH Releases 3 Studies Linking Glyphosate to Cancer, Contradicting EPA
content:
The National Institutes of Health (NIH) has released three studies that link glyphosate, the active ingredient in the widely used pesticide Roundup, to cancer. The findings directly contradict a recent Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) conclusion that glyphosate is not a carcinogen.  

Experts have noted that the NIH research raises concerns about the influence of chemical companies on the EPA’s pesticide division. The studies could have significant political and legal fallout, especially given the White House’s close relationship with Bayer, the producer of Roundup.  

The EPA is currently undergoing a court‑ordered re‑evaluation of glyphosate’s cancer risks. The new NIH findings add pressure on the agency to determine that the substance is linked to cancer, which would trigger a modest increase in regulations.
summary: The National Institutes of Health released three studies that link glyphosate, the active ingredient in Roundup, to cancer. These findings contradict an EPA conclusion that the weedkiller is not a carcinogen and may prompt a court‑ordered reevaluation and increased regulation.
author: Guardian Science

title: Caitlin Thomas recalls storm at music festival 270km north of Melbourne
content: Tens of thousands of people experience strikes each year. What are the effects of a current five times hotter than the sun – and how can you keep safe? Caitlin Thomas recalls knowing that something terrible had happened but not fully understanding what. She and her partner had arrived at a music festival some 270km north of Melbourne in the early afternoon and began setting up their tents and a gazebo for shade when the sky suddenly turned dark and the rain became incredibly heavy. A huge gust of wind picked up and Thomas asked her partner to hold on to the gazebo so it wouldn’t fly away. “He then asked me to hold on to it also so he could crack open his beer.”
summary: Caitlin Thomas and her partner were setting up tents and a gazebo at a music festival 270km north of Melbourne when a sudden storm rolled in. Heavy rain and a strong gust of wind forced them to hold onto the gazebo to keep it from flying away.
author: Guardian Science

title: NASA Launches NG-25 Mission to Send Space Crop Experiments to ISS
content:
NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division will send a suite of experiments to the International Space Station aboard Northrop Grumman’s 25th Commercial Resupply Services mission. The payload includes a first-of-its-kind space crop production system designed to help astronauts sustain themselves during long-duration missions. By understanding how crop production functions in microgravity, researchers aim to develop safe, nutritious, and reliable food sources for future habitats on the Moon and Mars.

The new prototype growth chamber will undergo testing to validate its water delivery mechanisms and optimize volume. Insights gained from this investigation are intended to inform the design of plant production systems for deep-space exploration. Additionally, the knowledge acquired may benefit terrestrial agricultural practices, including vertical farming and indoor growing systems.

Alongside the crops research, the mission carries a precision health investigation focused on human brain tissues. This experiment builds on previous work involving miBrains, which are small, lab-grown models of the human brain. The current study will validate a miniature fluid-handling system designed to mix, deliver, and maintain the nutrient-rich liquid required to keep these tissues alive.

The findings from the brain tissue research could help identify potential neurological risks associated with spaceflight and develop strategies to protect astronaut health. The investigation may also advance human tissue research and neurological disease modeling on Earth. These efforts align with the division’s goal of using space environments to conduct investigations that are not possible on Earth, thereby advancing fundamental scientific knowledge for both exploration and life on the planet.
summary: NASA’s NG-25 mission will carry a first‑of‑its‑kind space crop production system to the International Space Station aboard Northrop Grumman’s 25th Commercial Resupply Services flight. The experiments aim to validate plant‑water delivery, optimize volume, and advance crop‑production research that could inform future Moon and Mars habitats.
author: NASA News

title: Artemis III astronaut Andre Douglas visits Vehicle Assembly Building, sees RS-25 engine
content:
NASA astronaut Andre Douglas, an Artemis III mission specialist, visited the Vehicle Assembly Building at Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026. During the tour he stood inside an RS‑25 engine test article.

For Artemis III, four RS‑25 engines will power the Space Launch System’s core stage to launch the Orion spacecraft. Orion will conduct critical rendezvous and docking tests with lunar lander systems in low Earth orbit, advancing the capabilities needed before astronauts return to the lunar surface on Artemis IV.
summary: Artemis III astronaut Andre Douglas visits Vehicle Assembly Building, sees RS-25 engine.
author: NASA News

title: WebOS Community Edition 3.2.0 provides first OTA update for Palm/HP TouchPad
content:
WebOS Community Edition 3.2.0 has become the first over‑the‑air update for Palm/HP’s TouchPad, a device that is 15 years old. The update modernises the hardware and brings the original webOS experience back to the classic tablet.

The developer’s work also includes Lunacy, a sibling project that delivers the webOS interface and apps to Android devices. In addition, Luna DE is a developer tool that packages the webOS app contract into an SDK‑compatible Electron app, allowing developers to target Mac, Windows and Linux platforms.
summary: WebOS Community Edition 3.2.0 provides first OTA update for Palm/HP TouchPad.
author: Hacker News

title: Show HN: bouncemarket launches live prediction market game for a bouncing ball
content: A ball will fall. Trade on where it lands. I made this game! Some technical details: The entire drop of the ball is simulated server-side, then streamed to each client as server-sent events with a small buffer. Every drop is deterministic from its starting position, so rounds can be replayed exactly for later analysis, but tiny variations in starting position can change the ultimate outcome. There's some AI traders to keep the market moving, but they drop out in any round that has more than five people. They operate using a naive set of rules that I wrote for them, so they're not too hard to beat -- it's when the market is full of real people that it gets tricky. Curious to get feedback on anything you would change, and especially whether the mechanics were clear right away or not. Comments URL: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=50667726 Points: 304 # Comments: 95
summary: The game simulates a ball drop server‑side and streams the deterministic drop to each client via server‑sent events. It includes AI traders that drop out when more than five people join, and the creator is asking for feedback on the mechanics and clarity.
author: Hacker News

title: Physicist launches DragDropMath, a static site for learning math by dragging symbols
content:
A professional physicist has launched DragDropMath, a static web tool that lets users learn to simplify mathematical expressions and solve equations by dragging symbols. The interface permits only correct moves, allowing learners to “feel” the right steps without encountering incorrect ones. The creator notes that the idea stems from a personal observation made during a PhD program nearly two decades ago, when the symbols in equations seemed to have an inherent “physics” that guided proper manipulation.

The site operates without advertisements, trackers, or user accounts, and it stores progress locally in the browser cache. Teachers can generate custom problem sets, which are encoded directly in the link to the activity. The developer plans to expand the content to include chapters on trigonometry, complex numbers, and some calculus, while still determining the optimal mode of interaction.

Development of the mobile experience has recently begun, and the author acknowledges that some rough edges may remain. Feedback is being solicited for suggestions on content, bug fixes, and feature requests. The announcement has attracted considerable attention, earning 63 points and 15 comments on Hacker News.
summary: A professional physicist created DragDropMath, a static website that lets users learn to simplify expressions and solve equations by dragging symbols, allowing only correct moves. The site has no ads, trackers, or accounts, lets teachers create problem sets via encoded links, and the developer is adding mobile support while planning additional chapters.
author: Hacker News

content:

The article lists a mix of high‑end and budget‑friendly items, many of which have never been discounted before or have fallen below their usual price thresholds. The focus is on practical, everyday gadgets that enhance home automation, from lighting and audio to security and climate control.

A standout entry is the Govee Table Lamp 2 Pro X Sound by JBL, an RGB smart lamp that incorporates a JBL speaker and battery power. The lamp is available for $119.99 on Amazon, $139.99 at Best Buy, and $119.99 at Govee. LIFX offers a two‑pack of Everyday Smart Light Bulbs for $9.98 on Amazon, while the Alexa Photo Frame—a 10‑inch anti‑glare touchscreen that doubles as a smart speaker—can be purchased for $114.99 in black on Amazon or Best Buy, and $134.99 in walnut on Amazon. The Aqara Smart Lock U400, which unlocks automatically using UWB technology, is discounted to $199.99 on Amazon in both black and silver.

Birdbuddy’s Nook smart bird feeder is highlighted as the company’s most affordable model. It sells for $84.50 on Birdbuddy without a solar panel and $119 on Birdbuddy with solar. The Roborock Curv 2 Flow, a roller‑mop robot vacuum, is slashed to $549.99 on Amazon and $599.99 on Best Buy. Philips Hue Festavia string lights are offered for $185.23 on Amazon for the 65‑foot version and $280.47 for the 130‑foot version. The Skylight Calendar Max, a 27‑inch digital wall calendar, is available for $529.99 on Amazon and $519.99 on Best Buy.

Security and convenience gadgets also feature heavily. The Reolink Video Doorbell PoE camera is priced at $99.99 on Amazon, while the Aura Aspen photo frame, which displays images from Google Photos, iCloud, or a companion app, sells for $199 on Amazon. The Narwal Flow 2 robot vacuum is discounted to $899.99 on Amazon with an on‑page coupon, $949.99 on Narwal, and $949.99 on Wayfair. Lutron’s Diva Smart Dimmer Switch Kit can be found for $99.95 on Amazon, Best Buy, and The Home Depot. The Eve Energy Smart Plug, supporting Matter over Thread, is available for $28.95 on Amazon with a coupon.

The list concludes with a few high‑end items that have dropped below their usual price points. The Echo Dot Max, featuring Amazon’s AZ3 chip, is now $49.99 on Amazon, Best Buy, and Target. The Ecobee Smart Thermostat Premium is discounted to $189.99 at Costco with an extra SmartSensor, and the Roborock Saros 20 robot vacuum is available for $989.99 on Amazon and Roborock. The article notes that the list will be updated as more deals surface, encouraging readers to revisit frequently for the latest offers.

title: Oura to drop Android 11 support on Dec 8, 2026, risking data loss
content:
Oura has announced that it will stop supporting Android 11 on December 8, 2026. The company’s support page states that users who remain on Android 11 may lose access to all of their data if they do not upgrade to Android 12 or a newer version before the deadline.  

The page advises Android users to update to Android 12 or higher to avoid loss of data or features. If a user chooses not to upgrade, they may still be able to use some limited historical Oura App features, but the company warns that historical data will not carry over if the smartphone system is upgraded later. The notice reflects a common practice of ending support for older operating systems.
summary: Oura to drop Android 11 support on Dec 8, 2026, risking data loss.
author: The Verge

title: Apple second‑gen AirTags on sale for $18 at Amazon, Walmart and Best Buy
content:
Apple’s second‑generation AirTags are being offered at an all‑time low of $18 each on Amazon, Walmart and Best Buy. The devices, which normally list for $29, have been selling for about $24 since Amazon Prime Day in late June, making the current price a notable discount.

The new AirTags attach to keyrings, luggage and bags and include an upgraded ultra‑wideband chip and improved Bluetooth, which the source says expands the tracking range to 1.5 times that of the first‑generation model. Their internal speaker is described as 50 percent louder, helping locate items hidden in cushions or bags.

Even without the upgrades, the AirTags provide up to a year of battery life on a single coin‑cell battery and work with iPhones and newer Apple Watch models, offering Apple users a reliable way to track keys, luggage and other belongings.
summary: Apple’s second‑generation AirTags, normally $29, are being sold for $18 each at Amazon, Walmart and Best Buy. The new AirTags include an upgraded ultra‑wideband chip, improved Bluetooth, a speaker 50 percent louder and up to a year of battery life.
author: The Verge

title: Nothing CMF Buds 2A sell for under $20 on Black Friday
content:
Nothing’s ANC‑equipped earbuds are on sale for less than $20 for Black Friday. The Nothing CMF Buds 2A are available on Amazon in three colors. The black set starts at $17.89, which is about $11 below the MSRP. The light gray and orange sets are priced at $19.99 each, a $9 discount from the listed $29 price.  

The CMF Buds 2A deliver decent sound and active noise cancellation. They include customizable EQ settings, multipoint connectivity, and an IP54 rating for water and dust resistance. Battery life lasts up to eight hours before the earbuds need to be placed in the included USB‑C charging case.  

While they may not match flagship budget earbuds such as the AirPods 5 or Google’s Pixel Buds 2A in premium features or sound quality, the value proposition is clear. For under $20, consumers receive ANC, Google Fast Pair support, and robust durability suitable for light exercise and yard work.
summary: Nothing CMF Buds 2A sell for under $20 on Black Friday.
author: The Verge

title: Akai releases MPC Sample 1.4 firmware with developer mode and custom knob effects support
content:
Akai has released version 1.4 of the firmware for its MPC Sample, a compact and low‑cost sampler that the company says is becoming increasingly powerful. In this update the firm acknowledges the device’s growing use as a platform for “vibe‑coded” custom firmware and modifications, and it is now officially supporting that community.

The new firmware introduces several developer‑focused features. It adds compatibility with a new software development kit and allows users to install custom Knob Effects plugins by placing them in a designated folder on a microSD card; the plugins are then automatically listed at the bottom of the Knob Effects menu. Additionally, a Developer Mode has been added, enabling the execution of scripts on the device. Akai’s approach signals an embrace of the modding ecosystem rather than opposition to it.
summary: Akai has released the MPC Sample 1.4 firmware, adding developer features such as SDK support and custom Knob Effects plugins. The update also introduces a Developer Mode for running scripts and automatically recognizes plugins placed on the device’s microSD card.
author: The Verge

title: Allstate outage affects website, apps and roadside assistance since Nov. 23
content:
Allstate began experiencing a service outage on Monday, November 23, affecting its website, mobile applications and roadside‑assistance service. The disruption has persisted through the week, with customers still unable to access their accounts via the app or site as of Friday afternoon.

The company has not issued a detailed statement but directed reporters to a notice on its website. The notice states that Allstate customers can reach the company in several ways, including online, by phone and through local offices. It also notes that some access has been restricted for the past 48 hours, yet the company remains available to respond to customer inquiries. This outage follows similar disruptions at other firms, such as Microsoft and JPMorgan Chase, that have occurred in recent weeks.
summary: Allstate’s website, mobile apps and roadside assistance service have been down since Monday, November 23. As of Friday afternoon the services remained unavailable, and the company pointed customers to a notice saying they could still be reached by phone, online and local offices.
author: The Verge

title: Apple iPad Mini 2026 Now $100 Off on Amazon and Walmart for Black Friday
content:
Apple’s newest iPad Mini, reviewed in early November, carries a steep launch price of $699.  The first major discount appears on Black Friday: Amazon and Walmart both list the 2026 iPad Mini with Wi‑Fi and 128 GB of storage for $599, a $100 reduction and the lowest price the device has reached.

The 2026 model upgrades several key features.  It sports an 8.5‑inch OLED display that delivers deeper blacks and better contrast than the 8.3‑inch LCD on the previous generation.  Despite the larger screen, the tablet is smaller and lighter, and Apple has added IP67 dust‑ and water‑resistance.  In a review, David Pierce noted that the new durability made him feel more comfortable handing the Mini to a spill‑prone toddler, keeping it in the kitchen while following recipes, or even taking it into the shower to watch a football game.

Performance also improves.  The A20 Pro chip loads apps faster and runs demanding games more smoothly, while battery life remains around nine hours of screen time.  At $599 the device is still pricey for basic web browsing or streaming, and the previous‑generation Mini—running the A17 Pro chip—can be found for under $500 if the OLED screen and water resistance are not essential.  The Black Friday discount therefore makes the newer model a more compelling upgrade for those seeking Apple’s smallest tablet.
summary: The 2026 iPad Mini is available for $599 on Amazon and Walmart, a $100 discount from its original $699 price. It features an 8.5‑inch OLED display, IP67 water resistance, and an A20 Pro chip, but remains pricey for basic browsing or streaming.
author: The Verge

title: Autobots' Origin Story Links Black Friday to Optimus Prime's 2005 Sacrifice
content: Every year has a Prime Day—some years even have two Prime Days!—where we celebrate the life and achievements of the greatest leader the Autobots have ever known: the inimitable Optimus Prime. But just as every dawn is twinned by a dusk that steals its light, so too did Optimus Prime's bright spark fade, extinguished by the foul hand of Megatron during the Great Decepticon Incursion of 2005. It is a day that lives in infamy forever, and we all know the tale—how the evil Megatron (cursed be the flow of his energon!) commandeered an Autobot shuttle, cruelly murdered its crew, and launched a cowardly surprise attack against Autobot City—a plan utterly bereft of honor, as was so typical of Megatron's schemes. Even as individual Autobots strove to secure Autobot City— heroes, all of them!—hope began to fade under an onslaught that included an attack by the fearsome Devastator, against which there appeared to be no defense. And then, at the precipice of disaster, Optimus Prime made the fateful declaration whose words still ring out to this day: " Megatron must be stopped, no matter the cost." The fearless Autobot transformed, rolled out, and got the job done—even though that cost was high. Many brave Autobots besides Optimus Prime lost their lives during the fighting. It was truly a dark day, a black day—and so, every year on the Friday after Thanksgiving, we pause to remember the noble sacrifices made by Prime and by so many others. This is why today is known as Black Friday. Read full article Comments
summary: The article describes Black Friday as a remembrance of Optimus Prime’s sacrifice during the Great Decepticon Incursion of 2005, when Megatron attacked Autobot City. It explains that each year on the Friday after Thanksgiving Autobots honor the fallen Autobots and Prime’s declaration to stop Megatron.
author: Ars Technica

title: Dominik Diamond calls this the biggest video‑game month while playing a 2006 Wii title
content: While everyone else is giddy over Zelda and GTA, Dominik Diamond finds himself behind the times on a Nintendo Wii I find myself on the wrong side of gaming history this month. I have zero zeitgeist. My takes are as fresh as something found at the rear of the fridge. I haven’t even played Grand Theft Auto VI yet, but we’ll get to that. Worse, all month, the Nintendo sector of the gaming world has been going googly eyed over Zelda. The Ocarina of Time remake seems to have produced more joy than all the puppies in the world. But not for me. I have never liked Zelda. It’s like being a movie reviewer who doesn’t like Disney, or a vegan shark.
summary: Dominik Diamond describes the current month as the biggest ever for video games. He notes that while others are excited about Zelda and GTA, he is playing a 2006 Nintendo Wii title and says he has never liked Zelda.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Global cybercrime group “the Com” threatens children, FBI says thousands involved
content:
The FBI estimates that thousands of people identify as members or recent members of the Com, a group linked to indecent images of girls and blackmail. Though the name “Com” is short for the Community, crime agencies worldwide warn it is far from benign.

The group’s young cybercriminals are causing havoc and putting children at chilling, sickening risk, according to those agencies.

Beau‑Jack Mensforth was jailed by a UK judge on Friday for his activities as part of the Com. He operated from his bedroom in north‑east England, and police urge parents to be aware and to check their children’s devices.
summary: The FBI estimates thousands of people identify as members or recent members of the Com, a network linked to indecent images of girls and blackmail. A UK judge jailed Beau-Jack Mensforth for his activities in the Com, and police are urging parents to check their children’s devices.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Top 10 cordless vacuum cleaners ranked after tests of 18 models
content:
A new review has examined 18 leading cordless vacuum cleaners from various manufacturers to determine which models deliver the strongest overall cleaning performance. The tests applied identical cleaning scenarios to each unit, measuring how well they captured dust, crumbs, mud, pet hair and other dry debris, as well as evaluating ease of use and user enjoyment.

Based on the results, the review identifies the ten cordless vacuums that consistently removed the most mess and proved the most convenient to operate. The article positions these ten models as the top‑rated choices for anyone seeking a reliable, long‑lasting cordless cleaner for everyday household spills and shedding.
summary: The article reviews 18 leading cordless vacuum cleaners and identifies the ten best performers. The tests measured cleaning ability, ease of use, and durability to determine the top favourites.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Hackers breach US Air Force's Cloud One platform, risking tactical data
content: Reuters reported on Friday that hackers have breached the U.S. Air Force’s flagship cloud‑computing platform, Cloud One. The intrusion, according to the agency, could jeopardize the security of sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data stored on the system. The breach was noted to have occurred days after reports emerged that a CIA database had been accessed. No further details about the attackers or the extent of the compromise were provided.
summary: Hackers are reported to have breached the US Air Force’s flagship Cloud One cloud computing platform. The intrusion could jeopardize the security of sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data.
author: Guardian Technology

title: London’s Cake and Bake Show honours David Attenborough centenary
content: London’s Cake and Bake Show is marking the centenary of broadcaster David Attenborough. Bakers in the city have presented nature‑inspired pieces, including lifelike gorilla figures and miniature sugar sculptures of Attenborough, as part of the celebration.
summary: Bakers at London's Cake and Bake Show are honouring David Attenborough's centenary with nature‑inspired creations. The displays feature lifelike gorilla figures and miniature sugar sculptures of the broadcaster.
author: Euronews

title: Russian drone strikes damage Ukraine energy, rail, civilian sites, halt exports
content: Russian drone strikes hit Ukraine’s energy, rail and civilian infrastructure, causing deaths. In the wake of those attacks and the arrival of winter cold, Ukraine halted all electricity exports, and electricity imports rose to their highest level since mid‑June.
summary: Russian drone strikes hit Ukraine's energy, rail and civilian infrastructure, causing deaths. The attacks and winter cold forced Ukraine to stop all electricity exports, with imports rising to their highest level since mid‑June.
author: Euronews

title: Belarus leader Lukashenka says Putin's logic would return Russia to Mongolia
content: Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko said that, by Putin’s logic, Russia should be returned to Mongolia. He added that medieval history cannot justify territorial claims because Russian lands were once under Mongol rule and that East Slavic statehood traces to Kyivan Rus’. He later softened his remarks, saying Putin perfectly understands this and is misinterpreted.
summary: Lukashenka said medieval history cannot justify territorial claims because Russian lands were once under Mongol rule and East Slavic statehood traces to Kyivan Rus'. He later softened his remarks, saying Putin perfectly understands this and is misinterpreted.
author: Euronews

title: Uzbek teacher's recycling project wins first place in global competition
content: An Uzbek teacher transformed a school recycling challenge into a green‑education project in Namangan that has reached 25,000 people across 25 schools. The initiative secured first place in an international competition that received 369 applications from 94 countries.
summary: The green education initiative developed in Namangan has reached 25,000 people across 25 schools. It took first place in an international competition that attracted 369 applications from 94 countries.
author: Euronews

title: Iranian twins Taraneh and Rumina tortured; Taraneh sentenced to death, Rumina 25 years
content: Relatives allege that Iranian twins Taraneh, 21, and Rumina were beaten and tortured while in custody. Rights groups report Taraneh was held in enforced disappearance for more than three months and forced to confess, leading to a death sentence, while Rumina received a 25‑year prison term after their arrest in Isfahan on 24 January. Both twins were shortlisted for the Sakharov Prize.
summary: Taraneh, 21, was held in enforced disappearance for more than three months and tortured into a confession, rights groups say. She was sentenced to death and her twin Rumina to 25 years in prison after their arrest in Isfahan on 24 January, and both were shortlisted for the Sakharov Prize.
author: Euronews

title: Estonia to close border with Russia on Dec 1, says FM Margus
content: Estonia has opened embassies in Baku and Yerevan as part of a move to strengthen its strategic ties with the South Caucasus. During a visit to Azerbaijan’s capital, Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said the Baltic nation will close its border with Russia on 1 December.
summary: Estonia has opened its embassies in Baku and Yerevan to strengthen its strategic ties with the South Caucasus. Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna confirmed during his visit to the Azerbaijani capital that the Baltic state will close its border with Russia on 1 December.
author: Euronews

title: Amnesty: Iran's justice system now catastrophic as protesters face death sentences
content:
Amnesty International reports that, amid a war with the United States and Israel, Iranian protesters are receiving death sentences after trials described as “grossly unfair” and tainted by torture. Iranian‑Canadian human rights lawyer and Amnesty researcher Raha Bahreini says the situation “has changed from bad to catastrophic,” noting that authorities are treating peaceful dissent as treason and espionage and that extrajudicial killings of peaceful protesters have occurred following the January 2026 protests.

Amnesty is urging the creation of an international criminal justice mechanism, potentially a special tribunal, stating that “there needs to be criminal accountability for these crimes against humanity.”
summary: Amnesty International says Iranian protesters are receiving death sentences after trials described as unfair and torture‑tainted amid the war with the US and Israel. The organization is urging the creation of an international criminal justice mechanism, possibly a special tribunal, to hold perpetrators accountable for crimes against humanity.
author: France 24

title: Spain's snap election pits Sánchez's PSOE against PP and possible PP‑Vox alliance
content: After eight years of socialist-led government, Spain is at a crossroads. Can Pedro Sánchez pull off another electoral comeback, or will the conservative Partido Popular make way for the far right into national government for the first time since the end of Franco's 40-year brutal reign? Just back from Madrid, Richard Werly, Europe correspondent for the Swiss daily Blick, joins Angela Diffley to examine the final days of campaigning and the generational divisions shaping Sunday’s snap elections. The youth are divided between the left and the far-right Vox party. Sánchez, nicknamed the “Teflon politician”, has campaigned heavily on housing and social issues. “We may see an outgoing prime minister performing better than expected,” says Werly.
summary: After eight years of socialist‑led government, Spain is holding snap elections with Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez campaigning on housing and social issues. The race features the conservative Partido Popular, the far‑right Vox, and discussion of a potential PP‑Vox alliance amid a youth split between the left and Vox.
author: France 24

title: ILO finds women‑dominated jobs twice as likely to face AI‑driven losses
content:
The term FOBO—fear of being obsolete—has emerged as people consider how artificial intelligence is reshaping the workplace. As AI technologies spread, many ask whether the impact will differ between women and men.

According to the International Labour Organization, occupations dominated by women are nearly twice as likely to experience job losses due to generative AI compared to those dominated by men. This finding highlights a gendered dimension in the potential economic effects of AI advancement.
summary: The International Labour Organization reports that occupations dominated by women are nearly twice as likely to be exposed to job losses from generative AI compared with male‑dominated occupations. The finding highlights growing fear of being obsolete, referred to as FOBO, as AI spreads.
author: France 24

title: The End of Spain’s ‘Frankenstein’ Coalition? Presidential Plotting in Paris, Kushner & Kremlin Trap
content: Catch up with the World This Week with Gavin Lee. In just 45 minutes, make sense of seven extraordinary days in global affairs, as Gavin and his handpicked panel of four leading international correspondents unpack the stories shaping the world — and the questions behind the headlines.
