title: Avi Davidson becomes first trial participant to use nerve‑connected prosthetic hand at home
content: Over the last few weeks, I’ve been talking to Alexander (Avi) Davidson. There are a lot of remarkable things about Avi. He sustained a horrific injury as a teenager, which left him paralyzed and without a left hand. Today, he uses his own experience to guide his practice as a trauma therapist. He’s also taking part in a clinical trial of some new tech that allows him to move—and feel with—a prosthetic hand. Unlike standard prosthetics, this one connects directly to nerves in Avi’s arm. He literally has wires coming out of his arm to plug it in with. Avi’s the ninth person to trial this tech. But he’s the first to take it home and use it independently, for things like drinking from a cup (which is not easy ) and writing (also not easy ). What struck me the most over our conversations was Avi’s outlook and approach to not just his injuries and learning to use this cutting-edge technology, but to life itself. He has learned how to use something like seven different prosthetics in the 17 years since his accident. By taking part in this trial, he’s had to fit hundreds of hours of lab-based training and physical therapy around his demanding job. He had surgery to implant electrodes in his arm and will eventually need another to remove them. And he won’t even get to keep the latest prosthetic long term. “While it’s unfortunate at times, and irritating at times, I do not regret what has come from [the accident], or the fact that it happened,” he told me. “I am not going to benefit from this … I wanted to be a part of this in the context of being able to help push the technology forward.” The research team at the University of Utah that is running the trial hopes it will answer longstanding questions about the technology. How does it fare in a real-world setting, outside of the lab? What do people end up using it for? Where can improvements be made? There may be some surprises along the way. Avi has found that his prosthetic wrist can feel sore and stiff when it’s been overused, just like his flesh-and-blood wrist. Weirdly, that feeling can be relieved by stretching it out. What’s going on here? No one really knows. Scientists don’t know whether Avi’s brain will change as a result of using the bionic hand, either. Before the trial started, they performed brain scans to see how his missing left hand was represented in his brain. Will that change? And what might that mean for people who are born without limbs—how might a bionic limb affect their brains? Avi will have the device until late January 2027 at the least, and potentially for another year. After that? Again, no one knows. It will depend on how the research is progressing, how Avi feels, and how much funding the team can secure. As a result, it’s not clear how long the device might even be expected to last in a person’s body. I’ll be following this study, though, and will keep you posted. This article first appeared in The Checkup, MIT Technology Review’s weekly biotech newsletter. To receive it in your inbox every Thursday, and read articles like this first, sign up here.
summary: Over the last few weeks, I’ve been talking to Alexander (Avi) Davidson. There are a lot of remarkable things about Avi.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: MIT Technology Review Opens 2027 Innovators Under 35 Competition
content:
MIT Technology Review has opened the nomination window for its 2027 Innovators Under 35 competition. The editors will annually select 35 young scientists, entrepreneurs, and inventors who have made significant contributions to fields such as human disease, climate change, and other pressing societal challenges.  

Candidates must be under 35 years old as of October 1, 2027, meaning they must have been born on or after October 2, 1992. Nominations can be submitted for individuals anywhere in the world who have produced a major finding or advance and can demonstrate real‑world impact. The nomination process is free and takes only a few minutes; nominations must be received by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on Tuesday, January 19.  

After the deadline, MIT Technology Review editors will review all nominees and select a group of semifinalists. Those semifinalists will be invited to submit a formal application, after which a panel of expert judges will evaluate the applicants and determine the finalists. More details about the selection process are available on the review’s website.  

The Innovators Under 35 list began in 1999 and has become an annual exercise that helps the review’s reporters identify the brightest young minds in the fields they cover. Subscribers can view the 2026 list and explore the full archives. The review looks forward to receiving nominations for the 2027 class.
summary: Every year, the editors at MIT Technology Review select 35 of the world’s top young scientists, entrepreneurs, and inventors to honor as our newest class of Innovators Under 35. And starting today, our 2027 competition is officially open for nominations.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: MIT Technology Review opens Innovators Under 35 nominations; bionic hand trial probes brain
content:
The MIT Technology Review has announced that the 2027 Innovators Under 35 competition is now open for nominations. Each year the review selects 35 of the world’s brightest young scientists, entrepreneurs, and inventors for its Innovators Under 35 list. The 2027 edition seeks researchers and founders who are engineering solutions to society’s most formidable problems, from human disease to climate change, as well as those who have made clever and useful inventions, important new scientific discoveries, or technological breakthroughs early in their careers. Nominees may be based anywhere in the world but must be under 35 on October 1, 2027. The newsletter provides instructions on how to submit a nomination.

The same edition of The Download also highlights a story from The Checkup, the weekly biotech newsletter, about a bionic hand that could offer new insights into the human mind. The story follows Avi Davidson, who suffered a horrific injury as a teenager that left him paralyzed and without a left hand. Davidson now works as a trauma therapist and is participating in a clinical trial of new technology that allows him to move—and feel—with a prosthetic hand. Prior to the trial, researchers scanned his brain to examine how the missing left hand was represented in his neural circuitry and to assess whether that representation might change with the use of the prosthetic. The article discusses what a bionic hand might reveal about the mind and what the findings could mean for people born without limbs.

Both pieces appear in the same daily edition of The Download, which is described as a weekday newsletter that delivers a daily dose of what’s happening in technology. The Innovators Under 35 announcement and the bionic‑hand story are presented as separate items within the newsletter, each linked to its source—MIT Technology Review for the competition and The Checkup for the prosthetic‑hand feature.
summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Our 2027 Innovators Under 35 competition is now open Every year, MIT Technology Review honors 35 of the world’s brightest young scientists, entrepreneurs, and inventors in our Innovators Under 35 list.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Americans Create Repair Cafés in Churches and Warehouses to Combat Throwaway Culture
content: Americans are establishing Repair Cafés in church basements and warehouses, creating cozy yet radical spaces where neighbors gather to help one another repair broken items instead of discarding them, thereby confronting a throwaway culture.
summary: Americans are building cozy yet radical spaces in church basements and warehouses. These spaces encourage people to fix broken items instead of throwing them away.
author: Wired

title: Our Favorite Merino Wool 30% Off in Unbound Merino Black Friday Sale
content: WIRED has identified its favorite merino travel T‑shirt as the best travel T‑shirt, and it is being offered at 30 % off in the Unbound Merino Black Friday Sale. The discount is available only until the sale ends tonight.
summary: WIRED’s pick for the best travel T‑shirt is on sale for Black Friday. The Unbound Merino sale offers 30% off the merino wool item and ends tonight.
author: Wired

title: Beats 360 headphones $100 off for Black Friday
content:
Black Friday is bringing a wave of discounts to a broad selection of wireless earbuds, over‑ear headphones and bone‑conduction models. Apple, Beats, Soundcore, Sony, Nothing, Bose and several other manufacturers are listed with reduced prices that span sub‑$100 options to premium headsets still marked down from their regular cost.

The Beats 360 headphones are highlighted as $100 off their original price this week. Described as ANC headphones suited for gym use, they are Beats’ first IP‑rated cans, feature removable ear cushions and are said to stay in place during most exercises while delivering solid bass. The current listings show a price of $249 at Amazon and $249.99 at Best Buy, down from $349.99.

Other prominent reductions include Apple’s AirPods Pro 3, which are offered for $149 at Amazon and Walmart and $179.99 at Best Buy, down from $249. Soundcore’s Liberty 5 Pro earbuds are listed at $129.99 at Amazon, Anker and B&H Photo, reduced from $169.99. Bose’s second‑generation QuietComfort Headphones are shown at $199 at Amazon, $199 at Best Buy and $219 at Bose, down from $359. Sony’s WH‑1000XM6 headphones are priced at $348 at Amazon and Best Buy, reduced from $458.

Further deals span a range of styles: the Beats Studio Pro are $139.95 at Amazon (select colors) and $99 at Walmart (select colors), down from $349.99. Nothing’s Headphone 1 Pro is $319 at Amazon and Walmart, reduced from $399. Shokz’s OpenRun model is $89.94 at Amazon and $89.99 at Best Buy, down from $149.95. Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro appear for $169.99 at Amazon and $179.99 at Walmart, reduced from $249.99.

Overall, the Black Friday listings present discounts on many of the year’s top audio products, offering consumers options from budget‑friendly earbuds to high‑end over‑ear headphones at prices lower than their standard retail values.
summary: The Beats 360 headphones are discounted by $100 from their original price this week. Black Friday deals also include deep discounts on many other headphones and earbuds from brands such as Apple, Sony, and Bose.
author: The Verge

title: Apple Watch SE 3 discounted to $179 (40mm) and $209 (44mm) for Black Friday
content:
During Black Friday the Apple Watch SE 3 is being offered at reduced prices. The 40 mm GPS model is listed at roughly $179 on Amazon, Walmart and Target, a $70 discount that is $20 lower than its prior lowest price. The 44 mm GPS version is priced around $209 at the same retailers, also $70 off and $20 beneath its earlier low point.

The SE 3, launched more than a year ago, adds an always‑on display to Apple’s budget‑friendly wearable line. It shares several features with higher‑end models such as the Series 12, including double‑tap and wrist‑flick gestures, fast charging and on‑device Siri. The watch does not include advanced health sensors like blood‑oxygen monitoring or an electrocardiogram, and its battery life is modest compared with premium models. Because of its feature set and the current discounts, the SE 3 is recommended as the Apple Watch most people should consider buying on Black Friday.
summary: The SE 3 adds an always-on display to Apple’s budget-friendly wearable. | Photo: Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge During Black Friday, the Apple Watch SE 3 is on sale in the 40mm / GPS configuration at Amazon, Walmart, and Target starting around $179 ($70 off), $20 less than its previous lowest price.
author: The Verge

title: Sony, LG, and TCL TVs Over 50% Off for Black Friday
content:
Black Friday sales have arrived, offering significant discounts on televisions from major manufacturers including Sony, LG, TCL, Vizio, Hisense, Samsung, and Roku. The article highlights that while TVs are substantial purchases that can last for years, the current sales make it an opportune time to upgrade. Recommendations span various technologies, including RGB LED, OLED, and Mini LED, with the assertion that the featured models provide value commensurate with their reduced prices.

TCL’s flagship X11L SQD-Mini LED TV, described as the best TV the company has ever built, is available at steep discounts. Originally priced near $3,000 for the 75-inch model, it is now listed at $2,997.99 at Amazon. Larger 85-inch and 98-inch versions are discounted at Best Buy and Amazon, respectively. The article notes that the X11L offers blazing brightness and great color accuracy. Additionally, the TCL QM8L, which utilizes the same SQD technology for higher brightness and color but at a lower cost, is discounted significantly, with the 65-inch model dropping from $2,499.99 to $997.99 at Amazon.

LG’s B6E OLED TV, an entry-level variant of the B6 OLED, is featured for its four HDMI 2.1 ports, 120Hz refresh rate, and pixel-perfect contrast. While lower brightness is noted as a compromise for the cheaper OLED, the 55-inch model is discounted from $1,399.99 to $699.99 at Best Buy. Sony’s Bravia 7 II, the company’s first RGB LED TV, is also heavily discounted. Despite a slightly reflective screen, it is praised for its picture quality and processing, with the 55-inch model reduced from $2,099.99 to $1,199.99 at Best Buy.

Other notable deals include the Vizio Mini LED Quantum 4K TV, which is highlighted for its privacy features and ease of use as a "dumb" TV, with the 50-inch model dropping to $198 at Walmart. Hisense offers discounts on both its 2026 CanvasTV, a 4K QLED model with a matte display and 144Hz variable refresh rate, and the U7SG mini-LED TV, which is noted for its brightness and reflection handling. The 55-inch CanvasTV is available for $697.99 at Amazon, while the 55-inch U7SG is listed at $599.99 at Best Buy.

Samsung’s S95H OLED, a winner of Value Electronics’ TV Shootout, features a glare-free screen and excellent color accuracy. Prices for the 55-inch model have fallen from $2,499.99 to $1,899.99 at Best Buy. Finally, Roku’s Pro Series 4K OLED TV is presented as an affordable option for gamers and movie enthusiasts, with the 55-inch model discounted from $999.99 to $699.99 at Amazon. The article suggests that these Black Friday offers provide a wide range of options for consumers seeking high-quality displays at reduced costs.
summary: Black Friday sales feature discounted prices on several Sony, LG, and TCL TVs, many of which are over 50% off their original prices. The article lists specific models such as TCL X11L, LG B6E OLED, Sony Bravia 7 II, and others, along with their reduced prices and key features.
author: The Verge

title: Grand Theft Auto VI features unique ending due to its couple-focused storyline
content:
Most Grand Theft Auto titles, like many open‑world games, let players continue exploring the map after the credits finish. The main story is treated as one segment of a larger, ongoing experience, with locations and side missions often remaining unvisited.

Grand Theft Auto VI departs from that pattern. According to producer Rob Nelson, the game’s narrative follows a couple who are trying to leave the criminal world permanently. Because the story’s focus is on that final break from crime, an open‑ended post‑credit world “didn’t make sense,” Nelson explained.

Consequently, GTA VI delivers an ending that aligns with its plot rather than preserving the usual open‑world continuation found in previous entries. This design choice reflects the game’s distinct storytelling approach.
summary: Grand Theft Auto VI does not leave its world open after the credits like previous entries, because its story follows a couple trying to leave a criminal life. Producer Rob Nelson said that type of ending did not make sense for this game.
author: The Verge

title: Oura Ring 5 drops to $299 for Black Friday, its biggest discount yet
content:
The Oura Ring 5 has slashed its price for Black Friday, dropping to an all‑time low of $299 on Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, and Oura’s own online store. The discount is $100 off the ring’s regular $399 price and is the largest markdown the product has seen.

Compared with the Ring 4, the new model is thinner, lighter, and more durable, making it more comfortable to wear during the day and while sleeping. It tracks sleep, activity, heart rate, and other health metrics just like its predecessor and offers roughly the same battery life and sensor set. The Ring 5’s charging case now supports wireless charging, though the case is sold separately for $99.

Oura has added several software features to the Ring 5. Health Radar monitors for significant changes in health, and users can import medical lab results, track GLP‑1 medications, and receive AI‑assisted medical guidance through a partnership with Counsel Health. A colleague, Victoria Song, noted that the Counsel Health feature makes it easier to connect with a doctor for quick medical questions, though it may not suit more serious concerns.

To access most health insights, users must maintain a $5.99 monthly Oura membership. Because the Ring 5 and Ring 4 are similar, Oura advises existing Ring 4 owners not to upgrade. However, for those new to smart rings, the Black Friday discount makes the Ring 5 an attractive option, only $50 more than the Ring 4’s starting price.
summary: The Oura Ring 5 is now priced at $299, a $100 discount, at Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, and Oura’s online store for Black Friday. The Ring 5 is thinner, lighter and more comfortable than the Ring 4 while offering similar health‑tracking features and battery life.
author: The Verge

title: Volvo lets drivers test updated 2028 XC60 and XC90 plug‑in hybrids with bigger batteries
content:
Volvo arranged travel and accommodation for Ars to drive its updated plug‑in hybrids, the XC60 and XC90. The Swedish automaker provided flights from Washington, DC, to Copenhagen, Denmark, and lodging so that Ars could test the vehicles. Ars notes that it does not accept paid editorial content.

Volvo’s product planners had originally envisioned the XC90, launched in 2015, and the smaller XC60, introduced in 2017, as the final models of their kind as electrification progressed. The anticipated shift to all‑electric vehicles, however, has not occurred as expected, particularly in the United States. Meanwhile, Europe and China continue to electrify, raising questions about investing in new replacements for models that may not have an eight‑year lifespan in many markets.

Instead of developing entirely new vehicles, Volvo has given the XC60 and XC90 a lifecycle refresh.
summary: Volvo provided flights from Washington, DC, to Copenhagen, Denmark, and accommodation so Ars could drive the XC60 and XC90 plug‑in hybrids. The 2028 refresh adds a much larger battery to the PHEVs along with updated infotainment and interior features.
author: Ars Technica

title: Ars staff share holiday gift picks for 2026, featuring books, bikes and gadgets
content: The holiday shopping season is upon us, and as is our custom, we're here with a list of Ars staffers' favorite recent purchases that could make good gifts. (Or maybe they might be a gift you get yourself!) Rather than try to write a definitive "best gifts for your sister or brother" type of guide, we simply polled Ars staffers on stuff they've actually bought this year that they recommend. The thinking is that if we're into it, hopefully some of you or your friends or family might be. As such, there's no rhyme or reason to these selections, really; it's just a list of stuff we bought that we're happy about. It's heavy on interesting books and cycling accessories, but there are some gadgets and the like in here, too. For each gadget (or whatever else it might be), we have a brief description of how or why we’ve been using this particular thing and why we would recommend it. Our picks are ordered by price, from lowest to highest. Note, though, that the prices of these products are listed as they were when the list was written. Online retailers often adjust prices frequently, especially around Black Friday, so just a heads up: The price might be different by the time you read this. Read full article Comments
summary: Ars staff compiled a list of their recent purchases to suggest holiday gifts for 2026. The selections, which range from books and cycling accessories to various gadgets, are presented in order of price with a disclaimer that listed prices may change.
author: Ars Technica

title: Intel pressured by Trump administration to give 10% stake or face unknown consequences
content: The message from the Trump administration to one of the world’s leading semiconductor companies was clear: Give the US government a chunk of your company. Right now. Or else. Do not make the “mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation,” Commerce Department lawyer David Shapiro told the chief financial officer of the Intel Corporation in August 2025, according to internal notes from a company call contained in a federal lawsuit. “The President is expecting to announce a deal on these terms on Friday.” Shapiro acknowledged that “the Board could choose not to accept the offer,” according to a summary of his remarks prepared for Intel’s directors. But the Trump administration official “noted that rejection will have consequences that [Shapiro] cannot predict.” Read full article Comments
summary: The message from the Trump administration to one of the world’s leading semiconductor companies was clear: Give the US government a chunk of your company. Right now.
author: Ars Technica

title: Independent developers craft GTA‑style games set in their own cities
content:
Independent game developers across Europe are adapting the open‑world, crime‑focused style popularized by Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto series to their own cities, from Helsinki to Istanbul, and doing so without the large budgets of major studios. The developers say they can place the series’ 3D template in any location that has people and enough cars to create the familiar chaos.

One example highlighted is Eamonn Swayah, who imagined a version of the original Grand Theft Auto set on a Manchester council estate. His concept includes local accents, left‑hand driving and a range of “hustle” activities, showing how the game’s mechanics can be re‑skinned for a specific neighbourhood.

The article notes that after the commercial success and controversy of GTA III, many “GTA clones” emerged throughout the 2000s and 2010s, demonstrating that the core open‑world formula can be transplanted to diverse urban settings.
summary: Independent developers are creating Grand Theft Auto‑style open‑world games set in locations such as Manchester and Istanbul. They say Rockstar’s GTA III template can be placed in any city with enough people and cars, a practice that spawned many “GTA clones” after the original’s success.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Meta launches UK AI shopping assistant Muse as retailers consider liability
content:
Meta is launching its Muse AI assistant in the UK this week, positioning it as a tool to find Black Friday deals, source Christmas gifts, and identify ingredients for romantic dinners. The company, which owns Facebook and Instagram, claims the launch will transform consumer shopping habits and retailer revenue streams.

While brands acknowledge that the use of such AI agents is increasing, they are unlikely to grant these tools full control over their sales processes. The rollout raises questions about liability, specifically asking who is responsible if the bot provides incorrect information or makes errors during the shopping experience.
summary: Meta launches UK AI shopping assistant Muse as retailers consider liability.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Best Black Friday deals under $50 highlighted by editors
content: We scoured hundreds of sales for the best deals below $50 on heated blankets, packing cubes, sleep masks and more Black Friday deals aren’t reserved for pricey vacuum cleaners and huge TVs. While many of us gravitate toward big-ticket items with steep discounts, it is also worth searching for sales on smaller purchases, from reusable water bottles to phone chargers. We combed through hundreds of deals to find 20 Black Friday deals under $50 worth a glance, from items for braving holiday travel to gift ideas rigorously tested by our editors. summary: Editors scoured hundreds of sales and selected 20 Black Friday deals under $50, including heated blankets, packing cubes and sleep masks. The guide also notes discounts on smaller items such as reusable water bottles and phone chargers.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Natural England objects to Avonmouth AI datacentre weeks before ministers threaten agency
content:
Natural England formally objected to a proposed 40 MW artificial‑intelligence datacentre at Avonmouth, urging Bristol City Council to refuse planning permission. The agency cited the risk the development poses to protected wildlife and habitats, noting that the site lies within 600 metres of one of the United Kingdom’s most important locations for migratory birds.

The objection was lodged weeks before ministers announced a threat to abolish Natural England, the independent environmental adviser. The timing links the agency’s intervention on the datacentre with the broader governmental discussion about its future.
summary: Natural England objected to a 40MW AI datacentre at Avonmouth near Bristol, warning that the project threatens protected wildlife, habitats and a key migratory bird site within 600 metres. The objection was made weeks before ministers threatened to abolish the independent environmental adviser.
author: Guardian Technology

title: AI agent completes first UK cardless purchase of Papa John’s pizzas
content:
An order of nine Papa John’s mini margherita pizzas has become the United Kingdom’s first purchase completed by an artificial‑intelligence agent using cardless payment technology. The transaction was carried out without the customer sharing bank security details and was conducted as part of a Financial Conduct Authority‑regulated sandbox trial. The trial involved Lloyds Bank and payment‑service provider TrueLayer.

The experiment highlights retailers’ growing interest in AI‑driven shopping assistants, a trend that is expected to expand as firms explore such technology ahead of high‑traffic periods like Black Friday.
summary: An AI agent made the first UK purchase using cardless payment technology when it ordered nine mini Papa John’s margherita pizzas. The transaction was part of the FCA’s sandbox trials and used Lloyds Bank and payment specialist TrueLayer, with no bank security details shared.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Labor leaders urge AI guardrails as Walmart's AI use harms workers
content: Labor leaders and consumer advocates are calling for safeguards as artificial‑intelligence tools become more common in U.S. retail operations. They say protections are needed for both workers and shoppers while AI use expands. On Black Friday, as millions of Americans begin holiday purchases, the impact of AI on the retail environment is already visible. Anna, a cashier at a Walmart in southern Oregon and a United for Respect leader who asked to stay anonymous over retaliation concerns, criticized Walmart’s AI implementation and its effects on employees.
summary: Labor leaders urge AI guardrails as Walmart's AI use harms workers.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Meta whistleblower Sarah Wynn-Williams urges Andy Burnham to expand NDA ban
content:
Meta whistleblower Sarah Wynn‑Williams has urged Andy Burnham to strengthen the ban on non‑disclosure agreements. She says tech insiders who raise concerns about AI are being silenced in a system she compares to George Orwell’s 1984.

Wynn‑Williams, who served as the director of global public policy at Meta—then called Facebook—has been unable to discuss a series of allegations about the company’s treatment of teenagers that she details in her memoir because of restrictions imposed by the company. She warns that insiders concerned about AI development need protection.
summary: Sarah Wynn‑Williams, who served as director of global public policy at Meta (formerly Facebook), said tech insiders raising AI concerns are being silenced. She urged Andy Burnham to go further in banning non‑disclosure agreements, noting she cannot discuss allegations in her memoir because of company‑imposed restrictions.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Iran denies responsibility for Kuwait drone strike that killed two Italians
content: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called the accusations baseless and the incident "suspicious" and offered to cooperate on a joint investigation. Kuwait called it "a heinous Iranian aggression". Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar and the UAE condemned the attack.
summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the accusations were baseless, called the drone strike suspicious and offered to cooperate on a joint investigation. Kuwait labeled the attack a heinous Iranian aggression, and Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar and the UAE condemned it.
author: Euronews

title: Man and dog swept by king tide at Cannon Beach, Oregon, escape unharmed
content: A video shows a man and his dog being pulled into the surf by a strong incoming wave at Cannon Beach, Oregon. Police had previously warned the man about the hazards of King Tides. Both the man and the dog escaped the water unharmed.
summary: A man and his dog were swept into the surf by a powerful incoming wave at Cannon Beach, Oregon, after the man had been warned by police about the dangers of King Tides. Both escaped the water without injury.
author: Euronews

title: Kim Aris relieved after first call in five years, questions Myanmar military motives
content: Kim Aris, the son of Myanmar’s Aung San Suu Kyi, told Euronews’ The World Conversation that he felt “relieved” to hear his mother’s voice for the first time in five years. He also urged tougher enforcement of sanctions and defended his mother’s record concerning the Rohingya genocide ruling.
summary: Kim Aris told Euronews’ The World Conversation he was relieved to hear his mother, Myanmar's Suu Kyi, speak after five years. He called for tougher sanctions enforcement, defended her record on the Rohingya genocide ruling, and questioned the military’s motives.
author: Euronews

title: North Korea suspends Russian military aid on Kim Jong-un's order, Kyiv reports
content: Ukraine’s military intelligence reports that North Korean leader Kim Jong‑un personally ordered a halt to Russian military aid. The decision followed remarks by Russia’s deputy foreign minister that the suspension could help ease tensions between Seoul and Pyongyang.
summary: Ukraine's military intelligence said Kim Jong-un personally ordered North Korea to halt its military aid to Russia. The move followed Russia's deputy foreign minister saying the suspension would help ease tensions between Seoul and Pyongyang.
author: Euronews

title: EU budget summit collapses amid dispute over spending and strategic tasks
content: The EU summit on the Union’s common budget for 2028‑2034 collapsed early, according to the announcement. Delegates were divided: some advocated protecting established spending, while others pushed for cost cuts and a focus on financing new strategic tasks. Foreign‑policy expert Alexander Wolf of the Hanns Seidel Foundation in Berlin warned that the disagreement exposes a deeper clash over Europe’s strategic priorities.
summary: The EU summit on the Union's common budget for 2028‑2034 has initially failed. Foreign policy expert Alexander Wolf of the Hanns Seidel Foundation said the dispute pits those who want to protect established spending against those who seek cuts to fund new strategic tasks.
author: Euronews

title: South Africa's anti‑immigration movements grow as foreigners face hardship
content: South Africa, once described as a welcoming refuge for people escaping conflict and persecution, is now seeing the experience of many foreign residents deteriorate, according to correspondents. Amid rising unemployment and broader economic hardship, anti‑immigration movements are gaining traction, turning the promise of a new life for thousands of foreigners into a growing nightmare.
summary: South Africa was once a welcoming refuge for people fleeing conflict and persecution. Now thousands of foreigners say life is becoming a nightmare amid unemployment, economic hardship and rising anti‑immigration sentiment.
author: France 24

title: Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party reaches preliminary coalition deal with left‑wing faction
content: Israel’s Gadi Eisenkot and the Yashar party have reached a preliminary coalition deal with a left‑wing faction on Thursday. The agreement follows a brief dispute that had threatened Eisenkot’s bid to unseat Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu after last month’s inconclusive election, according to France 24’s Andrew Hilliar.
summary: Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party and a left‑wing faction agreed on a preliminary coalition deal on Thursday. The agreement follows a brief dispute that threatened Eisenkot's bid to unseat Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu after an inconclusive election last month.
author: France 24

title: EU leaders fail to reach budget deal after 12‑hour summit
content: EU leaders at the bloc headquarters in Brussels on Thursday failed to agree after more than 12 hours of talks on the budget and a new $49 billion loan for Ukraine’s economic and military needs next year. France 24’s Dave Keating reports on the outcome.
summary: EU leaders at the Brussels headquarters on Thursday could not reach a consensus on the bloc's next budget after more than 12 hours of talks. The negotiations also involved a proposed $49 billion loan to support Ukraine's economic and military needs for the coming year.
author: France 24

title: Drone attack in Kuwait kills two Italian air defence technicians
content: A drone attack in Kuwait killed two Italian technicians working on an air defence system on Thursday, marking the first fatal strike in the Gulf state for months.
summary: A drone attack in Kuwait killed two Italian technicians who were working on an air defence system on Thursday. It was the first fatal strike in the Gulf state for months.
author: France 24

title: Spain election: Housing crisis and immigration dominate final campaign debate
content: Spain heads to the polls on Sunday for an early parliamentary election that could bring a right‑wing coalition to replace the Socialist‑led minority government of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, one of Europe’s last left‑ist leaders. The final campaign debate has focused on the housing crisis and immigration, as reported by correspondent Sarah Morris.
summary: Spain will hold an early parliamentary election on Sunday. The vote could bring a right‑wing coalition that would replace the Socialist‑led minority government of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez.
author: France 24

title: Ukraine residents brace for difficult winter as Russia targets energy infrastructure
content: Ukraine’s residents are bracing for another harsh winter as Russia continues to target the country’s energy infrastructure. The ongoing strikes and power cuts are expected to persist, while supply‑chain pressures are driving food prices higher. Many Ukrainians are either cutting back on essentials or stocking up in anticipation of the coming months.
summary: Russia is continuing to target Ukraine's energy infrastructure, prompting residents to prepare for a difficult winter of strikes and power cuts. Pressured supply chains have driven up food prices, leading many Ukrainians to cut back on essentials or stock up for the coming months.
author: France 24

title: Black Friday shifts from crowded in‑store sales to year‑long online promotions
content: Black Friday, once characterized by crowds queuing outside stores for single‑day bargains, has shifted to weeks of online promotions. As discounts now appear throughout the year, shoppers are growing more cautious about advertised offers and are increasingly using AI tools and price‑comparison services to locate genuine deals. Camille Knight examines the origins of this global shopping phenomenon.
summary: Black Friday has evolved from crowds queuing outside shops for one‑off bargains to weeks of online promotions. Consumers are becoming more cautious about advertised deals and increasingly turn to AI and price comparisons to find genuine bargains, according to Camille Knight.
author: France 24

title: Thanksgiving storms flood East Coast, knock out power and delay flights, parade postponed
content:
Severe storms struck the U.S. East Coast on Thursday, producing torrential rain, strong winds and coastal flooding. The weather left nearly one million homes without power and caused hundreds of flights to be cancelled and thousands delayed during one of the country’s busiest travel periods.  

The conditions also forced the postponement of New York’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade until Saturday.
summary: Severe storms hit the US East Coast on Thursday, causing torrential rain, strong winds, coastal flooding and leaving nearly one million homes without power. The weather also led to hundreds of flight cancellations, thousands of delays and forced New York’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to be postponed until Saturday.
author: France 24

title: Indian workers increasingly fill German labor gaps amid market challenges and scams
content: The number of Indians working in Germany has grown rapidly in recent years. However, many still face challenges in the labor market, and some fall victim to recruitment scams, leaving them vulnerable to exploitation.
summary: The number of Indians employed in Germany has risen rapidly in recent years. However, many encounter labor‑market challenges and some become victims of recruitment scams that expose them to exploitation.
author: DW World

title: Rodrigo Duterte's ICC trial in The Hague could affect powerful Philippine dynasty
content: Former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte is standing trial at the International Criminal Court in The Hague for actions related to his country’s war on drugs. The case also carries the potential to influence the political prospects of one of the Philippines’ most powerful dynasties.
summary: Former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte faces trial in The Hague at the ICC over his deadly war on drugs. The proceedings could also determine the political fortunes of one of the Philippines' most powerful dynasties.
author: DW World

title: Serbia arrests Informer TV owner Dragan J. Vucicevic amid media accountability debate
content: The arrest of Dragan J. Vucicevic, owner and editor‑in‑chief of Informer TV, has prompted discussion about Serbia’s approach to its pro‑Vucic media network. Observers are questioning whether the detention signals accountability for media figures aligned with the government or reflects another political power struggle.
summary: Dragan J. Vucicevic, owner and editor-in-chief of Informer TV, was arrested. The arrest has sparked debate over whether Serbia is holding the pro‑Vucic media network accountable or engaging in a political power struggle.
author: DW World

title: Gambia votes Dec 5 as President Adama Barrow seeks third term
content: President Adama Barrow is running for a third term as Gambians head to the polls on December 5. The vote will assess both the opposition’s appeal and the nation’s progress on democratic reform.
summary: President Adama Barrow is seeking a third term in the Gambian election on December 5. The election will test the opposition's appeal and the country's progress on democratic reform.
author: DW World

title: Support services prioritize survivors in gender‑based violence care
content: Reaching out for help represents a significant step for survivors of gender‑based violence (GBV). The article emphasizes that the experience survivors have after entering a support service can influence their journey toward recovery and safety, highlighting the importance of centering survivors in GBV service provision.
summary: Reaching out for help is an enormous step for survivors of gender‑based violence. What occurs after they enter a support service can shape their path toward recovery and safety.
author: UN News

title: King tides and storms batter US coasts, damage pier in Pacifica, California
content:
Heavy rain, strong winds and coastal flooding have created hazardous conditions for millions traveling during the Thanksgiving period, as king tides and large waves have battered both U.S. coasts. The severe weather has prompted concerns about safety for holiday travelers across the country.

Along the California coast, the king tides caused notable damage in Pacifica, located south of San Francisco. On Wednesday, large waves struck the shoreline, destroying part of a pier and sending debris into the ocean. The National Weather Service responded by issuing coastal flood warnings for portions of the Pacific coastline as well as for shorelines around San Francisco Bay and San Pablo Bay.

In Pacifica, several beachfront properties have already experienced flooding. Additionally, authorities in Marin County temporarily issued an evacuation warning for residents of beachfront homes at Stinson Beach. The combined effects of the king tides and storm conditions have heightened risk for coastal communities during the holiday weekend.
summary: King tides and huge waves have battered both US coasts during the Thanksgiving period, creating hazardous conditions with heavy rain, strong winds and coastal flooding. In Pacifica, California, waves destroyed part of a pier, flooded beachfront properties and prompted National Weather Service flood warnings and a temporary evacuation warning for Stinson Beach homes.
author: Guardian World

title: Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez says he cannot imagine losing election
content: Spanish prime minister Pedro Sánchez said “I can’t conceive of us losing,” expressing confidence in an election victory despite poll results. International coverage has often portrayed the Vox party as Franco nostalgists with ultraconservative Catholicism and civil‑war rhetoric toward Catalan separatists, according to a freelance journalist and Sobremesa podcast host based in Madrid.

title: Erin Patterson seeks high court leave to appeal triple murder convictions
content: Patterson, 52, seeks leave to appeal to Australia’s highest court over deaths of estranged family members after fatal beef wellington lunch Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Erin Patterson has applied to the high court seeking leave to appeal after a failed bid last month to overturn her triple murder conviction. summary: Erin Patterson, 52, has applied to Australia’s High Court for leave to appeal her triple murder convictions. She was found guilty last year of murdering her estranged husband’s parents, Don and Gail Patterson, and his aunt Heather Wilkinson after hosting them for a beef wellington lunch.

title: Police investigate chainsaw damage to 500-year-old “King Jarrah” tree in WA park
content:
Western Australian police are investigating the alleged criminal damage of a 500‑year‑old jarrah tree known as “King Jarrah” after it was reportedly chainsawed in Wellington National Park, a protected area south of Perth. The 36‑metre “iconic” tree, described by authorities as beloved, is the focus of a rapid response effort, with officials saying they are considering “all options” to preserve it.

Police announced on Friday that they have appealed to the public for information to identify the person or people responsible for the vandalism. The investigation remains ongoing as authorities work to safeguard the historic tree.
summary: Police are treating the vandalism of the 500-year-old “King Jarrah” tree in Wellington National Park as an alleged criminal damage incident. Western Australian authorities say they are considering all options to save the 36‑metre jarrah tree after it was chainsawed and have appealed for public help to locate the responsible person or people.

title: Grace Tame confronts ex-Murdoch executive Matt Handbury over rape remark
content: Matt Handbury, nephew of Rupert Murdoch, admits making offensive remark and says he was referencing assault survivor’s ‘strikingly attractive get-up’ Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast A former Murdoch media executive has admitted he said Grace Tame “must be looking to be raped again” at an event, after the former Australian of the year overheard the comment and confronted him. title: NSW coroner says Aboriginal man's 2023 custody death preventable; guard watched TV
content:
A NSW coroner concluded that the 2023 death of a 33‑year‑old Aboriginal man in custody at Silverwater was preventable and “one of the most egregious deaths” she had investigated. The coroner’s report notes that a prison guard was watching TV while the man was dying in custody.

In response, the coroner recommended that Corrective Services NSW overhaul officer training for self‑harm responses and ban officers’ access to TV and YouTube while on shift. A judge echoed this stance, calling for officers to be prohibited from screens and phones during their duties.
summary: The NSW coroner concluded that the 2023 death of a 33‑year‑old Aboriginal man in custody at Silverwater was preventable and one of the most egregious deaths she had investigated. She recommended that Corrective Services NSW overhaul officer training for self‑harm responses and ban officers from using TV, YouTube and phones while on shift.

title: Disney+ Offers $4.99/Month Bundle for Full MCU Ahead of Avengers: Doomsday
content:
Avengers: Doomsday, set for release on December 18, is described as the biggest Marvel release of the year. To better understand the film’s storyline and multiverse details, viewers are encouraged to catch up on previous content available on Disney+. The platform hosts the entire Marvel Cinematic Universe catalog, which includes key television series such as Loki, VisionQuest, and Thunderbolts, alongside previous Avengers films. These titles are highlighted as essential viewing for anyone seeking a working understanding of the lore before the new movie arrives.

For those new to the multiverse concepts, the source recommends starting with the TV show Loki and the movie Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. These titles are said to break down the rules of the multiverse, exploring concepts such as timeline branching, superhero councils, and incursions. Additionally, the Fantastic Four reboot and the recently released VisionQuest are noted for introducing Dr. Doom, the titular villain of the upcoming release. The article advises paying attention to post-credits scenes for key character reveals and suggests that the original 2000s Fantastic Four films, featuring Chris Evans as the Human Torch, may also be of interest.

Specific recommendations are provided for different levels of familiarity with the franchise. For a general lore breakdown of the multiverse, viewers should watch Loki, Doctor Strange, and The Fantastic Four reboot. For direct preludes to the Avengers: Doomsday storyline, Thunderbolts and VisionQuest are identified as the key titles. Thunderbolts is noted to directly precede Doomsday by 14 months, while VisionQuest bridges the gap to the film, leading into its prelude.

Disney+ is also promoting a Black Friday bundle deal that includes access to both Disney+ and Hulu for $4.99 per month for 12 months. This ad-supported bundle represents a 62% discount from the usual $12.99 price point. The subscription provides access to nearly every Marvel movie and series, as well as extensive non-Marvel libraries including Star Wars, Pixar, National Geographic, and Alien. Hulu content included in the bundle features shows such as Shōgun, The Bear, Paradise, and X-Files.

The premium version of the bundle is also discounted, dropping from $21.99 to $14.99 per month. The source states that the standard bundle saves subscribers $96 over the year, while the premium bundle saves $84. This offer is intended for new and lapsed subscriptions, as it is not applicable to existing Disney+ subscribers. For viewers less interested in Marvel, the bundle offers other sci-fi options like Alien: Earth and The Testaments, along with the entire Star Wars franchise.
summary: Disney+ Offers $4.99/Month Bundle for Full MCU Ahead of Avengers: Doomsday.

title: Dark Energy Camera captures striking blue Betta Fish Nebula in Centaurus
content:
The Betta Fish Nebula, a supernova remnant located approximately 6,800 light-years from Earth in the Centaurus constellation, has been featured in a new cosmic portrait. Formed by the explosion of a star significantly more massive than the sun, the nebula is a wisp of gas and dust that has expanded and collided with surrounding interstellar medium over time. This interaction has resulted in a glowing, blue cloud that resembles a fish, earning it its distinctive nickname.

The image was captured by the Dark Energy Camera (DECam), an instrument created by the U.S. Department of Energy. DECam is installed on the National Science Foundation’s Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope in Chile. While the camera is primarily designed to study the effects of dark energy, the mysterious force causing the universe’s expansion to accelerate, it is also capable of producing striking astronomical imagery.

DECam serves as a key tool for the Dark Energy Survey, a six-year international collaboration that has gathered observations of hundreds of millions of galaxies and thousands of supernovae. Although initial results from this survey were revealed in January, scientists continue to use DECam to explore the nature of dark energy. These ongoing efforts are conducted alongside other instruments, including the recently launched Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, to further understand the cosmos.
summary: The Betta Fish Nebula is a supernova remnant located roughly 6,800 light-years from Earth in the Centaurus constellation. This image was captured by the Dark Energy Camera installed on the Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope in Chile.
author: Space.com

title: London Broncos target new venues and Australia‑friendly times after Super League return
content:
London Broncos are targeting new venues and Australia-friendly kick-off times, including Thursday and Saturday lunchtime slots, following their return to the Super League. The Rugby Football League awarded the club the 15th spot in the newly expanded competition for 2027. Last year, the Broncos dominated the Championship, losing only one league fixture and securing a domestic treble with a squad widely considered ready for the top flight.

The club’s strategy aims to grow rugby league while also campaigning to the NRL for a unique double-header against the Brisbane Broncos at Wembley in 2028. These initiatives represent part of a broader plan to establish a stronger presence in the sport’s highest tier.
summary: London Broncos target new venues and Australia‑friendly times after Super League return.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Steelers owner backs McCarthy, calls Rodgers' actions insubordination
content:
Pittsburgh Steelers owner and president Art Rooney II has expressed “100% confidence” in head coach Mike McCarthy following a public dispute with quarterback Aaron Rodgers. Rooney II characterized Rodgers’s recent actions as “insubordination” and stated that such outbursts could not be tolerated. The comments come after Rodgers was benched on Tuesday night and subsequently waived by the team.

The conflict escalated after Rodgers appeared on The Pat McAfee Show, where he accused McCarthy of falling asleep during a meeting. Rodgers further alleged that the head coach missed meetings and a walkthrough later that same week. These claims were corroborated by unnamed sources in a Wednesday report by ESPN.

With Rodgers no longer on the roster, the Steelers are preparing to face the Denver Broncos on Friday. Mason Rudolph is set to start at quarterback for the upcoming game.
summary: Art Rooney II expressed full confidence in head coach Mike McCarthy and labeled Aaron Rodgers' recent outbursts as intolerable insubordination. Rodgers was benched and waived after accusing McCarthy of falling asleep during a meeting, with the Steelers preparing to face Denver with Mason Rudolph at quarterback.
author: Guardian Sport

title: NFL roundup: 59-yard FG seals Eagles’ 21-point comeback against Cowboys; Bears beat Lions in classic
content: Jake Elliott kicked a 59-yard field goal with two seconds remaining to lead the Philadelphia Eagles to a 21-point comeback victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving. In another matchup, the Chicago Bears defeated the Detroit Lions, ending the Lions' winning streak in a game described as a classic.
summary: NFL roundup: 59-yard FG seals Eagles’ 21-point comeback against Cowboys; Bears beat Lions in classic.

title: Paris Fury retracts claim Tyson Fury diagnosed with schizophrenia
content:
Paris Fury has retracted her claim that her husband, boxer Tyson Fury, was diagnosed with schizophrenia shortly after his November 2015 victory over Wladimir Klitschko in Düsseldorf. The initial remark, which suggested the condition put the subsequent Joshua fight at risk of cancellation, appeared in an early version of a new Netflix documentary titled Disclosure.

In response to the clarification, Netflix stated it has worked to “update” the footage. The revised documentary is scheduled for release on Friday.
summary: Paris Fury retracted her statement that Tyson Fury was diagnosed with schizophrenia following his 2015 fight against Wladimir Klitschko. Netflix said it updated the footage of the documentary in light of her clarification.

title: Cricket Australia expands ball tampering forum to cover 2017-18 Ashes series
content:
Cricket Australia announced a new forum to let players and staff from the 2018 South Africa tour discuss the sandpapergate incident. The scope of the discussion has been expanded to cover the entire 2017‑18 season, including the Ashes series.  

The process will be independent and led by senior counsel Fiona McLeod. Participants can share their experiences in a “safe and confidential” environment, with the forum explicitly stating that there will be no sanctions or recrimination. The move follows renewed public interest in the ball‑tampering saga after the release of Usman Khawaja’s memoir earlier this month.
summary: The forum, led by senior counsel Fiona McLeod, will allow Australian players and staff to share experiences from the 2018 South Africa tour and the 2017-18 Ashes series in a safe and confidential environment. Cricket Australia announced the terms on Friday after the ball tampering saga resurfaced following Usman Khawaja’s memoir.

title: Jagiellonia Bialystok Secures Europa League Draw Against Sunderland
content:
The match finished in a Europa League draw, with a Reinildo error extending Sunderland’s woes. Jagiellonia Bialystok’s head coach Adrian Siemieniec said the trip to Wearside to face Premier League opposition was one of the biggest highlights of his career, noting his previous Polish title.

Jagiellonia’s players worked hard to avoid an anticlimax, highlighting Sunderland’s struggles in front of goal through intelligent defending. They responded to falling behind with an almost immediate equaliser, forcing Sunderland goalkeeper Robin Roofs into a series of demanding saves.
summary: Jagiellonia Bialystok's head coach Adrian Siemieniec praised the trip to Wearside as a career highlight after the team secured a draw against Sunderland. The Polish side equalised quickly after falling behind and kept Sunderland goalkeeper Robin Roofs busy with intelligent defending.

title: Thomas Frank earns first Crystal Palace win as McNeil cuts down Real Sociedad
content:
Crystal Palace secured their first win under manager Thomas Frank after a dramatic 1‑0 victory over Real Sociedad. The match had seen Palace trailing to a Mamadou Sarr goal, but the game swung in their favour 17 minutes from full‑time when Jon Martín was sent off for denying Jean‑Philippe Mateta an equaliser.

The French striker capitalised on the dismissal, converting a penalty to level the score. Dwight McNeil then finished the comeback, scoring after an own goal in Saturday’s loss to Coventry. The win came in Frank’s first home match since taking over from Pierre Sage.

Despite a Yéremy Pino penalty saved in stoppage time and several missed chances, Dean Henderson made a decisive late save to seal the result, reviving Palace’s Europa League hopes. The club now heads into Sunday’s crucial encounter with Hull with renewed confidence.
summary: Thomas Frank earns first Crystal Palace win as McNeil cuts down Real Sociedad.

title: Norrie defeats Struff in Davis Cup quarter-final opening match
content: British number two Cameron Norrie secured a 3‑set victory over Jan‑Len­nard Struff in the opening match of Great Britain’s Davis Cup quarter‑final tie against Germany, held in Bolgona. The win gave the British side a perfect start to the encounter.
summary: Cameron Norrie, British number two, beat Jan‑Lennard Struff in three sets in the opening match of Great Britain's Davis Cup quarter‑final against Germany in Bolgona. The victory gave Great Britain a perfect start to the tie.

title: Thanksgiving Storms Ground DC Flights, Cut Power to Over 850,000
content: A powerful coastal storm disrupted Thanksgiving travel in the Washington, D.C., area on Thursday, with heavy rain and winds causing flights to be halted at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA). The storm also knocked out power for more than 850,000 homes and businesses along the East Coast and in the Midwest. The Federal Aviation Administration issued a ground‑flight directive in response.
summary: A powerful coastal storm on Thanksgiving caused heavy rain and winds that grounded flights at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA). The storm left hundreds of thousands of homes and businesses without power along the East Coast and in the Midwest, affecting more than 850,000 people.

title: Petition of 290,000 Canadians urges expulsion of US Ambassador Pete Hoekstra
content: A petition signed by nearly 290,000 Canadians was formally presented to the House of Commons on Thursday, calling for the expulsion of U.S. Ambassador Pete Hoekstra. Canadian Green Party leader Elizabeth May introduced the nonbinding document, which urged Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government to declare the ambassador “persona non grata” and revoke his credentials.
summary: A petition signed by nearly 290,000 Canadians was formally presented to Canada’s House of Commons on Thursday. The Green Party leader Elizabeth May introduced the nonbinding petition, calling on Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government to declare President Trump’s ambassador “persona non grata” and revoke his credentials.

content: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum criticized U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration officials regarding their tip line, asserting it interfered with Mexico’s operations. content: Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed (D-Mich.) posted a video to social media on Wednesday offering advice for managing “spicier” Thanksgiving conversations. title: Genetic data improves prostate cancer risk assessment in PSA testing
content:
A new study from Karolinska Institutet, published in JAMA Network Open, shows that genetic information can help provide a more individualized assessment of prostate cancer risk among men who are undergoing PSA testing.

PSA is a protein produced by the prostate that can be measured with a blood test.

An elevated PSA level can be a sign of prostate cancer, but PSA levels can also be affected by other changes in the prostate.
summary: Genetic information can help provide a more individual assessment of prostate cancer risk among men undergoing PSA testing, according to a new study from Karolinska Institutet published in JAMA Network Open. PSA is a protein produced by the prostate that can be measured with a blood test.

title: Mayo transplant cardiologist outlines new detection and treatment advances for heart failure
content: Heart failure, a frequent complication of heart conditions, occurs when the heart cannot pump enough blood to meet the body’s needs, producing various symptoms. Cardiovascular diseases, which include heart failure, are the leading cause of death worldwide. Transplant cardiologist Jose Nativi Nicolau, M.D., of the Mayo Clinic in Florida, outlines recent advances in earlier detection and new treatment options for the condition.
summary: Heart failure is a common complication of heart conditions and occurs when the heart cannot pump enough blood to meet the body's needs. Transplant cardiologist Jose Nativi Nicolau of the Mayo Clinic in Florida describes advances in detection and treatment for heart failure.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Tumor architecture and heterogeneity shape colorectal cancer progression and therapy
content: Tumor architecture in colorectal cancer is highly heterogeneous, with cancer cells from the same patient exhibiting markedly different characteristics and behaviors. This tumor heterogeneity diminishes therapeutic efficacy, as cells in distinct states may respond variably to treatment interventions.
summary: Tumors exhibit significant heterogeneity, with cancer cells in a single patient showing markedly different characteristics and behaviors. This heterogeneity lowers therapeutic efficacy because cells in different states may respond differently to treatments.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Sisters first to receive repurposed drug for rare blood disorder after genomic sequencing
content: Sisters who share a rare blood disorder have become the first patients to be treated with a repurposed medication. A team of doctors and cardiovascular scientists identified the drug’s target through genomic sequencing, enabling the new therapy for the condition.
summary: Sisters first to receive repurposed drug for rare blood disorder after genomic sequencing.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Young hikers in Peak District and Leicester find friendship in walking groups
content: Young hikers are sharing how participation in walking groups has improved their wellbeing. The discussion spans outings from the Peak District hills to Leicester’s city parks, featuring several young participants who say joining these groups has helped them feel better.
summary: Several young people have joined walking groups that hike in the Peak District hills and explore city parks of Leicester. They say the groups help them feel better.
author: BBC Health

title: Scientists discover most distant quasar formed 630 million years after Big Bang
content: Scientists have identified the most distant quasar yet, a galaxy core whose black hole is accreting material slowly. The quasar dates to roughly 630 million years after the Big Bang, placing it near the universe’s dawn and setting a new record for earliest‑formed quasars.
summary: Scientists have discovered the most distant quasar yet. The quasar’s galaxy core hosts a slow-chomping black hole and dates to about 630 million years after the Big Bang.
author: Phys.org

title: Study reveals two amino acid transport mechanisms in rare disease protein
content:
Research has identified two distinct mechanisms by which a protein associated with a rare disease transports amino acids. The findings add detail to the understanding of how this particular protein moves amino acids across cellular membranes.  

Cells continuously exchange amino acids with their surroundings using specialized membrane transporters, a process essential for protein synthesis and many physiological functions.
summary: Researchers identified two mechanisms by which a rare disease-associated protein transports amino acids. Cells rely on membrane transporters to exchange amino acids with their environment for protein synthesis and other processes.
author: Phys.org

title: Learning facts from interest may require less mental effort than learning for money
content: Research suggests that learning facts out of interest may require less mental effort than learning them for money. The source notes that humans can be motivated intrinsically—doing something because it is interesting or enjoyable—or extrinsically—doing it to obtain a reward such as money, praise or a good grade.
summary: Learning facts out of interest may require less mental effort than learning them for money. Intrinsic motivation is doing something because it is interesting or enjoyable, while extrinsic motivation is doing it to obtain a reward such as money, praise or a good grade.

title: Iron law of oligarchy first proposed by Robert Michels in early 1900s
content: The “iron law of oligarchy,” a concept first articulated by sociologist Robert Michels in the early 1900s, asserts that over a sufficient period any group will inevitably come to be governed by a small minority. This idea has lingered for more than a century as a pessimistic challenge to democratic ideals.
summary: The iron law of oligarchy suggests that over time every group ends up ruled by a few. The concept was first introduced by sociologist Robert Michels in the early 1900s.

title: St. Jude scientists redesign protein to boost DNA insertion by CASTs
content:
Scientists at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital have identified the mechanisms enabling precise DNA integration into specific genomic locations using CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs). By investigating type I-F3 CAST, the team uncovered structural details that explain how this protein family successfully inserts DNA at precise target sites. These findings provide new insights for future genomic engineering approaches.

The research, which highlights the potential of genome engineering to treat and cure diseases, was published in Nature. The study offers a clearer understanding of how molecular machinery selects targets, contributing to the ongoing development of biomedical innovations in this largely uncharted field.
summary: Researchers at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital demonstrated that protein redesign increases DNA insertion activity of type I‑F3 CRISPR‑associated transposases. Their structural analysis explains how the CAST machinery selects precise genomic targets and offers insights for future genome‑engineering approaches, with the findings published in Nature.
author: Phys.org

title: UN says global maritime trade to see zero growth in 2026
content: The United Nations said Thursday that global maritime trade, which transports more than 80 % of the world’s goods, is expected to show zero growth in 2026. The stagnation is attributed to shipping disruptions and trade uncertainties linked to the war in the Middle East.
summary: Global maritime trade, which moves more than 80% of the world’s goods, is projected to stagnate in 2026. The United Nations linked the zero‑growth outlook to shipping disruptions and trade uncertainties arising from the war in the Middle East, according to a Thursday statement.
author: Phys.org

title: Molecular cage catalysts vary over 10,000‑fold in activity, researchers find
content: Chemistry researchers have developed a new way to identify and understand highly effective artificial enzyme-like catalysts using powerful "molecular cages" that mimic the behavior of nature's enzymes. These tiny, hollow molecular structures act like miniature reaction chambers to trap molecules and accelerate chemical reactions. The cages showed enormous differences in performance, with the best catalysts more than 10,000 times more active than the least effective ones.
summary: Chemistry researchers have developed a new way to identify and understand highly effective artificial enzyme-like catalysts using powerful "molecular cages" that mimic the behavior of nature's enzymes. These tiny, hollow molecular structures act like miniature reaction chambers to trap molecules and accelerate chemical reactions.
author: Phys.org

title: University of Bayreuth creates digital edition platform for German lute tablature
content:
German lute tablature, a notation that can appear to modern readers as a secret code, was developed specifically for the Renaissance lute and preserves dances, songs and other musical works popular roughly 500 years ago. This rich notational tradition provides access to a fascinating world of historical music.

Researchers at the University of Bayreuth, working within an interdisciplinary team of experts, are using a digital scholarly‑edition platform to render these lute‑tablature sources both readable and audible once again.
summary: German lute tablature is a Renaissance notation that preserves dances, songs and other works popular about 500 years ago. Researchers at the University of Bayreuth, working in an interdisciplinary team, are using a digital scholarly edition platform to make these sources readable and audible again.
author: Phys.org

title: Author releases “Learning to Play Vim” manual after four years of work
content:
A developer announced the release of a new book titled Learning to Play Vim. The author, who began using Vim more than ten years ago, created the manual to provide a step‑by‑step guide that starts with basic concepts and progresses to advanced features. After more than four years of work—reported as 2,987 focused pomodoros, equivalent to 1,244 hours—the book was completed and made publicly available.

The manual is organized into 21 chapters and includes 170 exercises with solutions, along with real‑life examples that demonstrate how Vim can be configured for individual needs. Each topic references the related Vim help pages for further reading. Configuration examples are provided in both Vimscript and Lua, catering to users of Vim and Neovim, while explicitly avoiding Neovim‑specific features such as treesitter or LSP.

A landing page for the book is hosted at https://themouseless.Dev/vim/, and a sample containing the full table of contents and the first three chapters can be viewed at https://themouseless.Dev/content/learning_to_play_vim_sample.... The announcement was posted as a Show HN entry on Hacker News, receiving 82 points and 25 comments.
summary: The author announced the release of a new book titled Learning to Play Vim, which took more than four years and 2987 focused pomodoros (1244 hours) to write. The book includes 21 chapters, 170 exercises with solutions, real‑life examples, and configurations in both Vimscript and Lua, covering common Vim and Neovim features.
author: Hacker News

title: Kuwait intercepts Iranian drones, injuring four, and diverts passenger flights
content:
Kuwait's military reported four injuries after detecting and intercepting hostile Iranian drones in its airspace.

In response, flights crossing Iraq toward the Gulf were given new headings ahead of Kuwait, shifting the international corridor.
summary: Kuwait's military said four people were injured after a number of hostile Iranian drones were detected and intercepted in its airspace. Flights crossing Iraq toward the Gulf were given new headings ahead of Kuwait, shifting the international corridor.

title: Russia launches missile and drone barrage on Ukraine, killing at least three
content: Russia launched a ballistic missile and a barrage of drones against Ukraine, killing at least three people. Ukraine’s air defences intercepted 87 Russian missiles and drones overnight on Thursday. In a separate action, Ukrainian drones hit a chemical plant that produces components for military explosives and a power station in the Stavropol region.
summary: Russia launched a ballistic missile and drone barrage on Ukraine that killed at least three people. Ukraine’s air defenses downed 87 Russian missiles and drones overnight, while Ukrainian drones struck a chemical plant and a power station in the Stavropol region.
